A journalist from Argentina has claimed that Liverpool have now entered negotiations with Alexis Mac Allister over a prospective new contract.

The midfielder has just over 18 months remaining on his current deal and has been vociferous about his disappointment at not being offered an extension earlier this year, having seen fellow 2023 arrivals Ryan Gravenberch and Dominik Szoboszlai extend their respective terms at Anfield.

The 27-year-old has been in terrific form for the Reds so far this season, to the extent that Troy Deeney even suggested that the performances of the 2022 World Cup winner could give his team ‘a chance’ of being involved in the Premier League title race.

On Tuesday evening, Argentine reporter Cesar Luis Merlo took to X with a significant update on Mac Allister’s situation at Liverpool.

The journalist posted: ‘Liverpool have opened contract talks with Alexis Mac Allister in an attempt to renew his deal, which expires in June 2028. Over the coming weeks, it will become clearer whether the talks are progressing positively or not.’

(Photo by Justin Setterfield/Getty Images)

We’d take these initial reports with a pinch of salt for now until such time that they’re corroborated by top-tier sources closer to home, but if indeed Merlo’s information is accurate, it’s a very positive sign for the Reds.

That Mac Allister was prepared to speak so openly about his frustration at not being offered a new contract until now would seem to indicate that he very much wants to remain at Anfield, and the transformative improvement in his performances from last season to this also supports that theory.

Even if contract talks with Mac Allister have indeed commenced, it’ll probably take some time before an agreement is formalised, but at least it seems that the relevant parties are finally in talks over potentially keeping the 27-year-old at Anfield for the long-term.

#2030. ‘I would be lying if I said…’ Sean Longstaff very honest on Newcastle United to Leeds United move

The independent voice of Newcastle United since 1988

Get your daily update and weekly newsletter by signing up today!

Get your daily update and weekly newsletter by signing up today!

On 18 July 2025, Sean Longstaff moved from Newcastle United to Leeds United.

The Geordie midfielder had been a mainstay under Eddie Howe and across the Premier League seasons of 2022-23 and 2023-seasons he had featured in 68 of the 76 league games, starting 58 of them.

However, in what proved to be his final Newcastle United season, Sean Longstaff only started eight Premier League matches across the 2024-25 campaign and made 17 mostly brief sub appearances.

In total, Sean Longstaff only played 788 Premier League minutes in that final NUFC season, the equivalent of less than nine full matches of minutes.

So at the age of 27, the midfielder left Newcastle United to get more regular first team football with Leeds United, the Elland Road club paying a reported £12m.

Having turned 29 last month, Sean Longstaff has been reflecting on how things have gone so far in the 16 months since he moved to Leeds United.

The former Newcastle player has only started 11 of the 48 Leeds matches in the Premier League since his move, including only one of 10 this season, spending most of his time watching from the bench…

Sean Longstaff speaking to The Official Leeds United Podcast: “I would be lying if I said it has been the easiest year I’ve ever had. It’s been a tough year. There has probably been times, at home especially, where you are not that nice to be around. Ultimately, I made the decision to come to Leeds. I took my family away from the comforts of being at their home. I have taken a newborn baby away from his grandparents to bring him down here for me to enhance my career. Obviously, at the minute, it’s not gone probably to the perfect plan. But I don’t think life ever does.”

Sean Longstaff is not giving up though: “I take training as serious as possible. Whether that’s the day after a game, whether it is during the week, you have got to train as if you’re going to play. Then ultimately, if you don’t play, that’s not in my control. I can’t control it. All I can control is making sure that I’m fit enough to play when I get a chance, make sure I’m sharp enough, make sure my mentality is right. If I get a chance I want to try and show what I can do, whether that’s for 30 seconds, come on at half-time, or whatever the case may be, I can’t control other people’s decisions, all I can control is the controllables.”

Sean Longstaff comparing and contrasting the two clubs: “It is not until you probably get down here, everyone says Leeds is a massive club, but until you get here, you don’t realise how big it is. I came with an expectation of ‘it’s going to be Newcastle’s this and Leeds is that’….hen you get in, you think ‘oh actually, Leeds is so similar. Apart from the kit, everything else felt exactly the same. Obviously the only difference is me being from Newcastle and not from Leeds, but actually got to know a lot of people from the city and…the way they speak about Leeds is the way I felt about Newcastle. The more you meet people, the more you realise it’s massive.”

#2029. Sky Sports unveil Newcastle United unfinished transfer business and Matthias Jaissle wish list

The independent voice of Newcastle United since 1988

Get your daily update and weekly newsletter by signing up today!

Get your daily update and weekly newsletter by signing up today!

A new report from Sky Sports claims to unveil the unfinished Newcastle United transfer business.

The broadcaster also naming what they believe the Matthias Jaissle ‘wish list’ to be.

This comes at a point where we are just over six weeks away from the January 2027 transfer window opening.

Sky Sports state: ‘Matthias Jaissle wants to add more goals to his team this January, with a No 9 and a No 10 top of his wish list.’

The report then adding: ‘Matthias Jaissle doesn’t have an out-and-out No 10 in his current squad, despite persisting with the 4-2-3-1 formation since he joined the club in the summer. Joe Willock and Yoane Wissa have both been deployed in that position so far, but neither is natural in that role.’

As for how likely it is that Matthias Jaissle will see a new No 9 and No 10 arriving in January…

Sky Sports reporting: ‘However, the chances of signing players for both positions are slim, unless Newcastle offset that with sales. The winter window is notoriously difficult to operate in, with difference makers being the hardest players to sign. Signing a player for one of those positions is likely to be as good as Newcastle can achieve, given the financial restraints. Jaissle wants to add experience in January, having lost a clutch of experienced players in the summer. This will be his first window to operate in, having arrived late in the summer.’

Sky Sports claiming: ‘Ivan Toney is one striker he admires and would like to sign, having managed him previously with Al Ahli, but he knows it is unlikely to make economic sense for a club trying to invest in younger players with high ceilings.’

The entire Sky Sports report doesn’t even mention the fact that it isn’t Matthias Jaissle who is selecting the signings, with Newcastle United now having given Sporting Director Ross Wilson control of which players are bought and sold.

The Ivan Toney stuff is just lazy nonsense, linking Matthias Jaissle to the striker just because he managed him at Al Ahli.

Ivan Toney is on reported wages of £20m a year and he is Al Ahli’s key striker.

Al Ahli are majority owned by Saudi Arabia PIF, the same as Newcastle United, but the idea they would be willing to sell him to United is laughable, especially at some kind of knockdown price. Even more ridiculous are those fans and people in the media who talk of the possibility of the Saudi club letting Ivan Toney come on loan to NUFC because PIF have majority ownership of both clubs.

The Saudi Arabia PIF, except in very rare cases, treat their business investments on an individual basis and they run independently of each other.

In this case, you only have to look at what happened with Matthias Jaissle to quickly understand how things work.

Al Ahli were furious when Newcastle United took their Head Coach, there was no PIF pulling of the strings.

United had to pay the full £9.5m release clause AND even then Al Ahli messed Newcastle United about further by delaying the paperwork needed to complete the move, meaning Matthias Jaissle wasn’t able to start work with NUFC until 18 days before Newcastle’s Premier League season kicked off.

#2028. West Ham Receive Double Boost Following Kanté’s Mali Success

West Ham United midfielder Mohamadou Kanté has helped Mali qualify for the 2027 Africa Cup of Nations following a 2-0 victory over Rwanda on Tuesday evening. It’s another significant milestone for the young Hammer, who has only just made his senior international debut, and the good news doesn’t end there.

Mali secured qualification with two matches to spare, thanks to goals from Modibo Sagnan and Gaoussou Diarra in Kigali. Kanté came off the bench in the 64th minute, having made his international debut in Friday’s 3-2 victory over the same opponents.

Mali are now guaranteed a place at next summer’s finals in Kenya, Tanzania and Uganda. And having discovered precisely when the tournament will take place, I have to say I’m absolutely delighted for Kanté. In fact, it’s double delight as far as I’m concerned.

First and foremost, massive congratulations to Kanté.

Having decided to switch his international allegiance from France to Mali, he’s already playing senior international football and now has a major tournament to look forward to.

It’s a tremendous achievement, particularly when you consider how quickly things have happened for him this season.

Kanté has been one of West Ham’s most impressive players, and his international recognition is thoroughly deserved.

As Claret & Hugh recently reported following his international debut, his performances for the Hammers have now been rewarded with an opportunity to establish himself on the international stage.

But there’s another reason I’m so pleased about this news, and it’s one that makes a massive difference from a West Ham perspective.

I’ve always disliked the fact that the Africa Cup of Nations has so often been plonked directly in the middle of the domestic football season.

As we saw during the last campaign, the losses of both our full-backs, Aaron Wan-Bissaka and El-Hadji Malick Diouf, had a massive impact on West Ham.

Hammers youngster Mohamadou Kanté will be playing in the AFCON

Indeed, I wrote about the problem before their departure for AFCON, when we were facing the prospect of losing two important defenders at a particularly difficult time.

It was hugely frustrating, and I’ve never particularly liked the idea of clubs losing key players for several weeks in the middle of their league campaigns.

But this time, thank goodness, it’s different.

The Confederation of African Football has confirmed that the 2027 tournament will take place from 19 June to 17 July, rather than during the winter months.

That means Kanté can enjoy the experience of representing Mali at a major international tournament without West Ham having to lose him in the middle of the Championship season.

Of course, there’s still the question of whether Kanté will even be at West Ham next summer. Who’s to say he’ll still be at the club next year?

But assuming he is, the timing means Scott Parker won’t suddenly have to manage without one of his most important midfielders for several weeks during a promotion campaign.

#2027. West Ham’s £18m Castellanos Problem Could Prove Difficult To Solve

Reports originating from Argentine journalist Renzo Pantich have suggested that Taty Castellanos wants to leave West Ham United and has already rejected a lucrative offer from Flamengo in favour of remaining in Europe.

Where in Europe, one may ask – and that’s a question no one knows!

Pantich’s claim has generated plenty of attention, but when you dig beneath the surface, it raises a lot of questions!

The suggestion appears to be that by rejecting Flamengo, Castellanos has demonstrated a desire to leave West Ham while remaining in Europe. Yet that conclusion ignores several important realities.

Firstly, Flamengo are reportedly facing financial difficulties with high transfer debts and sponsorship issues due to the Brazilian government banning football clubs from receiving payments from betting and online casinos.

The Brazilian midfielder reportedly accepted a sizeable wage reduction to join Flamengo. It seems highly unlikely that Castellanos, who is approaching what should be the peak years of his career, would be prepared to make a similar sacrifice.

Flamengo’s interest in the striker is nothing new. The Rio giants admired him during his time at Lazio but were unable to make a deal happen because the finances simply didn’t work. The transfer fee and salary package required were beyond what they were prepared to pay. Indeed, it was suggested at the time the player wanted to remain in Europe – sounds like a déjà vu moment!?

Taty wants to leave but who can realistically afford him?

Lastly, and most importantly, there is no mention of any transfer discussions between West Ham and Flamengo on any news wires.

Nobody doubts the emotional attraction. Castellanos has never hidden his admiration for the Argentine giants, and a move back home would undoubtedly appeal on a personal level. The problem is affordability.

Matching a transfer fee acceptable to West Ham while also covering the striker’s wages would represent a huge financial commitment, even for one of South America’s biggest clubs. As C&H has previously reported, River Plate simply can’t afford the player.

In fact, C&H exclusively revealed that it is West Ham who have been actively exploring ways of finding a buyer for the underperforming forward rather than the player agitating for a move.

Despite accepting a wage reduction following West Ham’s relegation, Castellanos remains on a highly attractive contract. His current deal runs until 2030 and includes a one-year club option.

Even following the Championship wage reduction, he is still earning only marginally less than the reported £48,000 per week he received at Lazio.

Should West Ham return to the Premier League this season and want to activate that extension, Castellanos could still have effectively four years of Premier League-level earnings ahead of him.

At around £77,000 per week, that’s potentially close to £18 million in future wages.

Those are numbers very few clubs outside England’s top flight can realistically match.

There will almost certainly need to be compromise from both sides. West Ham appear keen to move the striker on, while Castellanos may have to accept that replacing those wages elsewhere will be extremely difficult.

For all the speculation, one thing seems clear: finding a buyer may prove considerably harder than finding rumours!

I have been a season ticket holder since the late eighties, so experienced the highs and lows of being a West Ham supporter. I previously wrote for OLAS and have contributed to a number of football publications in the past.

#2024. “Grim Reading” West Ham’s London Stadium Financial Problem Just Got Worse

West Ham supporters hoping that relegation to the Championship might bring some financial relief to the London Stadium’s troubled finances may be in for a shock.

The latest accounts for London Stadium LLP, covering the year ending March 2026, reveal an operation still struggling financially, with annual losses of £20.6m, negative net assets of almost £247m and a staggering £243.7m provision for expected losses under its long-term contractual arrangements.

While the figures represent an improvement on the previous year, the stadium remains heavily dependent on financial support from the Greater London Authority and, ultimately, London taxpayers.

But perhaps the most significant revelation for Hammers supporters is the financial impact of relegation.

The biggest concern in the accounts is an onerous contract provision of £243.7m.

In simple terms, this represents the stadium operator’s estimate of future losses from its long-term contractual commitments, principally its concession agreement with West Ham and its access agreement with UK Athletics.

The provision has increased from £206.7m in March 2024 to £241.5m in March 2025 and now £243.7m.

It is not a bill that needs paying immediately, but it highlights the scale of the financial challenge facing the stadium.

The London Stadium financial figures make for grim reading

The accounts explicitly acknowledge the financial consequences of West Ham dropping out of the Premier League.

The stadium’s financial forecasts currently assume the Hammers will return to the top flight after just one season in the Championship.

Should West Ham remain outside the Premier League for another season, the estimated contractual loss provision would increase by a further £2.3m.

That is a sobering admission and demonstrates just how important Premier League football is to the stadium’s financial model.

London Stadium generated revenue of £13.6m during the year, including £4.8m received from West Ham for its use of the ground.

However, this is nowhere near enough to make the operation financially sustainable.

The accounts confirm that the stadium continues to rely on Greater London Authority funding, with a capital contribution of £21.876m received during the year.

The GLA has also provided a letter of support covering at least 12 months from approval of the accounts.

In other words, despite being home to a Premier League football club for almost a decade, the stadium remains dependent on public-sector financial backing.

There was also an interesting development in the long-running financial dispute between West Ham and London Stadium LLP.

The disagreement concerned a payment of approximately £3.6m, plus interest, connected with Daniel Křetínský’s investment in West Ham.

Following a legal battle and an appeal, London Stadium ultimately won the case, with the money released from escrow in April 2026.

The accounts reversed a £3.941m provision previously made for the dispute, helping improve the reported financial result.

There are clearly significant challenges ahead.

The stadium’s financial future depends on West Ham returning to the Premier League, attracting new commercial partnerships, maintaining GLA support and managing its expensive long-term contractual commitments.

The recent departure of chief executive Graham Gilmore after nine years in the role adds another layer of uncertainty, with operations director Darren Raczkowski stepping in as interim chief executive.

For West Ham supporters, there is an uncomfortable irony.

The club’s move to the London Stadium was supposed to provide a modern home and a platform for growth, while delivering a lasting legacy for London.

Yet almost a decade later, the stadium is still losing millions, carries an enormous long-term contractual burden and remains reliant on public money.

And with West Ham now in the Championship, the financial assumptions underpinning the stadium’s future are already under greater pressure.

The big question is how much longer London taxpayers will be expected to support an operation that has yet to demonstrate it can stand on its own two feet.

#2023. West Ham Boss Parker Makes January Admission On talkSPORT

West Ham United manager Scott Parker has made it clear that January transfers are not currently at the forefront of his thinking, despite the Hammers’ obvious need to strengthen their squad. Asked directly whether West Ham would have money to spend and bring in fresh faces, Parker acknowledged that the January window would be considered if necessary. However, he explained that since arriving at Rush Green, his attention has been almost entirely focused on his players and coaching staff.

Personally, I think he’s absolutely right. Even with the best will in the world, and assuming West Ham bring in some brilliant players in January, there are still nearly two months’ worth of results to fight for with the players currently available. Parker would be absolutely mad to spend too much time concentrating on transfers now.

Speaking during his talkSPORT interview, Parker explained that he had barely spoken to anybody outside his immediate coaching environment since taking charge.

“I’m sure there’ll be an eye in January if need be,” he said, before explaining that his main priority was establishing the habits and principles he wants from his players.

West Ham have a director of football in Nils Koppen, who can deal with precisely this type of thing. There is no reason for Parker to be spending his first few weeks in the job obsessing about transfer targets when the current squad desperately needs coaching.

After all, Claret & Hugh has already revealed that Koppen is working on January recruitment, including an approach to a potential striker signing.

The work is happening behind the scenes, and Parker doesn’t need to be personally involved in every conversation.

Parker can outsource his transfer concerns to Koppen

As Claret & Hugh has already revealed following contact with the football club, January business is being planned.

Every message we’ve received from sources inside the club indicates that promotion back to the Premier League is the overwhelming priority.

Of course, I expect funds to be made available in January. That doesn’t mean West Ham have unlimited money to spend, but the club’s determination to get promoted has been made abundantly clear.

And whilst we’ve previously reported on the financial constraints surrounding January recruitment, that doesn’t mean the club will simply sit on its hands.

But the January transfer window cannot rescue the points we fail to collect in November and December.

That is why Parker is right to concentrate on coaching.

Another interesting aspect of the interview was Parker’s discussion of the mentality required to succeed in the Championship.

He explained that players coming down from the Premier League have often spent months losing football matches, only to find themselves suddenly expected to win almost every week.

That psychological transition, he suggested, can be enormous.

The players clearly have ability, but Parker needs to establish the mentality and habits that allow them to produce it consistently.

If he can do that over the next few weeks, West Ham will be in a considerably stronger position when January arrives.

And if Koppen can then strengthen the areas that need improving, all the better.

For now, though, I’m delighted Parker is concentrating on the job immediately in front of him.

Kris Gonzo (commonly known to the West Ham community as Gonzo) is the co-founder of Hammers Chat (established 2014) and the lead video content creator and columnist for Claret and Hugh.

With over a decade of professional sports media experience, he is a frequent West Ham United analyst and contributor for Sky Sports News, BBC Football Focus, and BBC Radio 5 Live. He previously served as an official video and content creator for West Ham United FC during the club's tenure at Upton Park and featured in the official documentary commemorating the historic final game at the Boleyn Ground.

A lifelong Hammer since the legendary 10-0 victory over Bury, when he isn't providing daily match analysis on the Hammers Chat YouTube Channel or broadcasting on X (@GONZObignose), he can be found walking his dog and restoring classic pinball machines.

#2022. 6 duels won, 4 key passes – ‘Mad’ Liverpool beast enjoys ‘brilliant’ performance for his country

One Liverpool player has been praised for his ‘brilliant’ performance for his country on Tuesday night.

Hungary’s two UEFA Nations League matches over the past week have been overshadowed by the fallout from Dominik Szoboszlai admitting that he played through the pain barrier for his country, a decision which hasn’t gone down well among some on Merseyside.

His club and international teammate Milos Kerkez was also in action for Marco Rossi’s side at home to Northern Ireland last night, and the 23-year-old’s efforts didn’t go unnoticed among the media.

Hungarian football writer Bence Bocsak took to X shortly after the final whistle in Budapest, where the match finished in a 1-1 draw, to praise the Liverpool left-back’s performance.

He posted: ‘Milos Kerkez was brilliant for Hungary tonight. The Liverpool man created the most chances in the game (4) and won the most tackles (2). Also won 6/7 duels and made 10 passes into the final third – the most on the pitch.’

Want more Empire of the Kop coverage? Add us as a preferred source on Google to your favourites list for news you can trust

While there was frustration for Kerkez and Szoboszlai over the result, which saw the Magyars miss their shot at automatic promotion to League A and instead face a two-legged play-off next March, the Liverpool defender can be especially pleased with his own contribution on Tuesday.

The figures below from Sofascore – some of which were also cited by Bocsak – illustrate the combative and creative attributes that the 23-year-old showed for Hungary last night.

Kerkez has started the bulk of our Premier League matches so far this season, even if at times he can still be overly impetuous to the extent that, after an accidental collision with Florian Wirtz against Bournemouth in September, Jamie Carragher described him as ‘a bit mad’.

However, he should take heart from his strong outing for his country, and Liverpool will need him to be even more assured and influential when Manchester United come to Anfield on Sunday.

It’d be the perfect occasion for our number 6 to deliver a statement performance and show that he can mature into being an integral presence in Andoni Iraola’s project on Merseyside.

#2021. Glasner made to wait for first win as Trafford thwarts Forest

James Trafford became the record signing for a British goalkeeper this summer and he is already proving invaluable for Leeds United.

Signed from Manchester City for an initial £40m in August, Trafford has made an outstanding start and frustrated Nottingham Forest twice in four days.

The England international secured his second successive clean sheet in this City Ground sequel to underline why Leeds moved to eclipse the previous record for Jordan Pickford.

“England’s No 1” was a frequent chant from the travelling Leeds fans and although it may take some time for him to dislodge Pickford as the country’s first-choice, he is loving life at his new club.

Trafford produced a number of fine saves and goals from Daniel James and James Justin secured a comfortable Carabao Cup second-round victory for Leeds, who also won here in the league on Saturday.

Dan James has put Leeds ahead against Nottingham Forest 💥 pic.twitter.com/BdiYMXFJ5h

Leeds manager Daniel Farke said: “He has the potential to be one of the best goalkeepers in the Premier League and that is why Thomas Tuchel has picked him for England.

“I like his natural confidence and aura, he knows that he’s good and he will be outstanding one day.

“He has major chances to be under the spotlight and we are very pleased with him so far.”

Forest manager Oliver Glasner will be pleased to see the back of Leeds. He was appointed by Forest for the primary reason of winning trophies after successful tenures with Crystal Palace and Eintracht Frankfurt, but this particular avenue is now closed for this season.

Four-time League Cup winners, Forest endured a difficult evening following the pre-match news that they have agreed a £45m deal with Chelsea for striker Liam Delap.

Forest have established a reputation for noisy transfer windows but are determined to focus on quality over quantity this year. With Delap to undergo a medical on Wednesday, Forest will then focus on signing a new right wing-back before the deadline.

Newcastle’s Jacob Murphy has been discussed, though a move is now regarded as unlikely. There are understood to be other targets under consideration.

Glasner has insisted he does not want Forest to panic, and it remains to be seen whether they do spring into life on the final day. He said: “I am not a magician or the messiah and we cannot ignore the reality that Leeds are ahead of us at the moment.

“For nine months last season we were fighting relegation, so the players know it is going to take a lot of work. I know exactly what we have to change and that is what we will do.

“We are responsible and made so many mistakes. Maybe we needed this result. At the moment we are far away from what we want but we will get there.”

This was a more open game than the attritional encounter from last weekend, as Trafford was forced into a fine early save to prevent Ola Aina’s cross from arcing into the top corner.

Yet both teams were frequently making mistakes and providing masterclasses in how to misplace passes, frustrating their respective managers in the technical area.

The most impressive moment of the first-half came from Leeds centre-back Joe Rodon, racing back into position to deny Chris Wood from close range. Rodon celebrated the tackle as if it were a 30-yard screamer.

It was always likely to be a mistake which proved the pivotal moment, and Arnaud Kalimuendo’s poor header cost the home team in the 50th minute.

Kalimuendo’s error presented Sean Longstaff with space to run into and his pass found James, who beat Matz Sels with a clinical finish.

“Can we play you every week?” was the inevitable chant from the travelling Leeds supporters.

Forest’s fans were becoming twitchy and Trafford produced another save to frustrate Wood from eight yards after a break down the right from Kalimuendo.

Glasner responded by making a quadruple substitution on the hour, yet Leeds remained dangerous and added a second goal 15 minutes from time when Justin bundled home after a goalmouth scramble.

Ethan Ampadu's long throw causes CHAOS in the Forest box as Leeds go 2-0 up! pic.twitter.com/CtGDDIaRNp

You can catch the draw for the next stage of the League Cup on Sky Sports Main Event tomorrow night after the conclusion of Preston North End vs Everton.

Nottingham Forest have agreed a club-record deal worth £45m for Chelsea forward Liam Delap.

Delap has been deemed surplus to requirements at Stamford Bridge, and while the clubs were in talks over an initial loan deal, they have now struck a permanent agreement for the striker.

The 23-year-old​ only signed for Chelsea in a £30m deal from Ipswich Town 12 months ago​ ​and is scheduled for a medical on Wednesday​. He will become Forest’s most expensive signing with the deal eclipsing the £37.5m they paid for Omari Hutchinson last summer.

Oliver Glasner has prioritised the addition of a new forward and Delap was a long-term target for the Austrian since his time as Crystal Palace head coach.

Delap held talks with Forest last year over a potential move, and was also understood to have spoken with Glasner while he was at Palace.

Speaking to ITV after the win, Rodon said: “I thought we were a bit sharper going forward, maybe a bit naive in the first half. I thought we had a lot of good chances maybe could have scored a couple of goals but we know it’s a difficult place to come and overall very happy to keep a clean sheet and win the game.”

Of his last-ditch tackle in the first half, he added: “We love it, as defenders it’s as good as a goal. I’m delighted, [keeping] clean sheets is my job and overall I got it right in the end.”

"There's a healthy arrogance about Leeds""Farke has gone from strength to strength"Izzy Christiansen and Jobi McAnuff praise the impact of Daniel Farke at Leeds 📈 pic.twitter.com/fgzLWRk3U2

"It's a bit soon to say Wembley!" 😅James Justin and Dan James react to Leeds progressing into round three of the Carabao Cup 🎙️ pic.twitter.com/m81C6eJT7C

And that is it. Two home defeats by Leeds in less than 80 hours for Forest. Glasner will have much to ponder with a daunting trip to Anfield coming up on Saturday. All smiles for Farke’s side.

A look at a third for Leeds. Aaronson drives forward before setting Wilson who in turn lays on a first-time pass to Calvert-Lewin. The forward attempts to take his shot first time but can’t get the requisite power on the ball to beat Sels.

A pitch invader makes a brief appearance on the turf but is swiftly ushered away.

There is a late chance for Forest. Hutchinson’s cross is helped on by Dominguez but that touch inadvertently takes the ball away from Ndoye at the back post.

Forest fans are filing out of the exits and who can blame them?

That just about sums up Forest’s night. Dominguez stands over a free-kick from a dangerous area and, with the box loaded with their most imposing aerial threats, the midfielder sends the ball well over their heads and out for a goal-kick. So poor.

Calvert-Lewin is now on for Nmecha. Not really the striker Forest defenders would want to see at this stage of the game.

Another set-piece, this time a Stach corner, is barely dealt with by Forest.

There’s a shout for a handball at the other end as Ndoye spears a cross into the body of Elvedi, but the referee rightly waves the appeals away.

The “oles” ring out from the away end as Leeds string a series of passes together in the corner right in front of it. Forest are looking rather helpless here.

Nottingham Forest 0 Leeds United 2 (Justin) Ampadu launches a throw-in from the right but has to reload as the referee notices some pushing in the box. His next attempt is far too loopy but causes Forest all sorts of trouble, bouncing and bobbling, and coming all the way through a thicket of limbs to Nmecha at the far post. Williams attempts to keep the ball out from a prone position on the goalline under pressure from Justin, who gets the final touch as the ball is bundled over the line.

It's messy but Leeds won't care! 😁Forest fail to deal with the throw-in and Nmecha is there to bundle it in...#EFL | #CarabaoCup pic.twitter.com/oV46fs5RmP

Jair goes into the book after catching Ampadu in full flight. He never had a prayer of reaching that ball.

The resulting free-kick lands to Amapadu himself in the box, but his effort is deflected behind for a corner which is not up to much.

Goalscorer James is taken off for Bogle, who will offer more mettle down Leeds’ right side as Forest search for an equaliser in the closing stages.

Stach has only been on the field for a matter of seconds but comes within a few inches of scoring. Wilson does well on the edge of the box before laying the ball to Stach whose curled effort grazes the outside of the side-netting.

Longstaff’s final contribution to this game is a foul and yellow card as he spreads his legs wide to stop Ndoye breaking away through the middle.

He is replaced by Wilson, as Tanaka and Okafaor also make way, for Stach and Aaronson.

There’s plenty more endeavour down Forest’s new-look left side. Hudson Odoi scampers down that flank before cutting inside, and while he’s unable to fashion a chance the intent is correct.

The substitutions appear to have breathed life into this Forest side. Murillo picks out Dominguez charging forward and Trafford does well to tip the midfielder’s effort behind. The resulting corner comes to nothing.

Glasner resolves he has seen enough and rings the changes. Diomande, Aina, Jesus and Kalimuendo are replaced by Murillo, Netz, Ndoye and Hudson Odoi.

Okafor shows off his dancing feet in the Forest box, pulling off a few stepovers before the ball comes to Ampadu on the edge of the area but his strike is dragged wide.

Chances at both ends! Kalimuendo plays a wonderful ball into the box for Wood to sweep home but Trafford springs into action and makes a stunning save.

Leeds go up the other end, Okafor profiting from a diversionary run from centre-back Elvedi but cannot find the target and double Forest’s lead.

End-to-end football! ⚡️First Wood, then Okafor - just 19 seconds between the two chances 😮#EFL | #CarabaoCup pic.twitter.com/TGQmtwLNwE

Leeds are ahead and the inevitable chant from the away supporters is “can we play you every week?”

This is of course their second meeting in four days and Leeds are on course to record the double.

Forest’s fans are starting to get a little twitchy.

Dan James puts Leeds United in front! ⚽️Tidy finish from the Welshman... #EFL | #CarabaoCup | @LUFC pic.twitter.com/GzWg6zLGLm

Nottingham Forest 0 Leeds United 1 (James) We finally have a breakthrough. Kalimuendo gives the ball up cheaply in the middle of the park and Longstaff is there to pick up the pieces, darting infield before laying on a perfectly weighted for James to gallop on to, take a touch and sweep beyond Sels. The winger has been Leeds’ biggest threat and deserves that goal.

James finds space down the right - again - and his cross is closed down and deflected behind for a corner.

Longstaff’s floated delivery is tipped away by Sels, but it turns out that the ball went out before coming in so a Forest goal kick is awarded.

A lovely rendition of Mull of Kintyre precedes a short blast of the referee’s whistle and we’re back under way...

Schlager goes into the book instantly for grabbing a handful of Tanaka’s shirt as the Japan international attempted to escape his clutches.

This hasn’t been much of an improvement from Saturday.

Both teams are producing masterclasses in how to misplace passes. Oliver Glasner and Daniel Farke have spent much of the first half looking very frustrated.

James Trafford must be feeling very comfortable and confident of a second successive clean sheet after joining from Manchester City.

Let’s hope for an improvement in the second-half.

Should the scores remain level after 90 minutes, we will go straight to penalties. There’s still a half to play of course, but Forest’s League Cup shoot-out record should be a source of confidence having won seven from eight.

What a tackle from Joe Rodon! 💥#EFL | #CarabaoCup | @LUFC pic.twitter.com/p5GkzSFEoZ

James wins the ball on the halfway line and feeds Okafor down the left. He attempts a deft through-ball into a thicket of bodies but it comes to nothing.

Leeds circulate the ball, working the ball from side to side but there is nowhere near enough movement in front of the ball-player for any meaningful forward passes to be played.

And, quite aptly, the referee blows up at three seconds past 45 minutes. Certainly not a half for the books.

Another half-chance for Forest! Milenkovic lands on a second ball off a deep free-kick but he cannot keep his strike down. A classic centre-half’s effort if you will.

Ampadu comes over to the left to fire in a long throw-in. Sels comes steaming out of his goal and fumbles the ball but is awarded a free-kick after Muharemovic makes contact. Looked very minimal in all fairness.

Oof, a good chance for Aina! Williams’ cross from the left comes all the way through to his opposite wing-back, but Aina’s half-volley sails over. A cracking contact, though.

Elvedi and Muharemovic look to be astute buys from Leeds’ perspective. Both assured at the back and the latter especially is confident progressing the ball.

Just as I type that Forest threaten with a ball over the top, but Justin nips in to take the ball away from Wood.

Another decent opening for Leeds after a Forest turnover. Nmecha strides through the middle but Milenkovic is in position to ensure his run comes to nothing.

What a tackle! Kalimuendo bursts through the middle after Leeds cede possession in a dangerous position. The winger plays in Wood who looks to be through on goal but Rodon comes out of nowhere to telescope a limb and stop the forward in his tracks. Fantastic defensive work from the Welshman.

Nmecha attempts to break beyond the halfway line but is stymied by a swarm of Forest players. He demands a foul from the referee who is not interested in the least.

It’s then Okafor’s turn to put in a dangerous cross from the left, but Nmecha cannot get to it.

Tanaka becomes the first man to go into the book. The ball gets away from him and Jesus puts body between man and ball smartly to win the foul.

Tanaka is now dropping into the back line to allow Leeds’ defenders the licence to get wider and higher. Forest will need to be wary of their opponents’ numerical advantage down the flanks.

The game has reached something of a holding pattern as both sides resolve to slow things down, at least temporarily. Forest have settled into a slightly deeper block.

Sensing an opportunity, Ampadu spins in a glorious through-ball between centre-back and full-back for James to gallop on to. He hits the by-line and cuts back to Longstaff, but the midfielder can’t beat Sels. A good chance that probably should have been converted.

A good chance goes begging! 🫣Longstaff is free for Leeds but fires it straight at Sels...#EFL | #CarabaoCup pic.twitter.com/0UJdfSDQ6w

Tanaka then turns provider, winning possession in Forest’s half before playing in Longstaff, whose cross-cum-shot does not threaten Sels’ goal.

Both sides have physical, quick out-balls, which has made for a frenetic encounter thus far. James rasps in another fierce cross from the right after another sweeping Leeds move, but Nmecha cannot get there and Tanaka fires well over on the follow-up.

Aina’s throw-in, this time from the left, is flicked on to Jesus at the back post and while the forward is able to direct the ball goalwards there is Justin on the line to clear the ball to safety.

Chance! Dominguez slides in Aina down the right channel and the full-back’s mishit cross has Trafford scrambling. He palms the ball behind for a corner, which is headed away for a Forest throw-in on the far side.

Leeds are enjoying a spell of possession here, Tanaka and Longstaff peeling off into the wide areas to collect the ball and disrupt Forest’s mid-block out-of-possession structure. The hosts are more than happy for Leeds to circulate the ball in front of their first line of pressure as, for the second time tonight, Trafford boots it out into touch.

Dominguez stands up a smart cross to the far post where Aina is waiting to head back across goal. Trafford backpedals into Kalimuendo and the referee awards Leeds a free-kick.

Wonderful touch there early in the game from none other than Oliver Glasner.

Forest’s head coach perfectly trapped a high ball as it landed towards him in the technical area.

James shows off his speed for the first time tonight, accelerating down the right before fizzing a dangerous ball into the six-yard box but Forest clear their lines.

Sels goes long to Wood (feels like the right play given his attributes), James lands on the second ball but can only boot the ball into row Z to jeers from the home fans.

Aina launches a long throw-in from the right and it’s headed behind for a corner. Trafford punches the inswinging delivery away and Williams’ effort from the edge of the box sails well over.

Forest are in their red home shirts, kicking from left to right. Leeds are in their yellow away number. Same set-up as the weekend.

Players and mascots walk on to the City Ground turf. A place in the League Cup third round on the line.

Oliver Glasner breaks his silence on Nottingham Forest's record signing, Liam Delap 🚨He speaks to @gabrielclarke05 ahead of Forest's Carabao Cup tie against Leeds 🗣️ pic.twitter.com/8DlWMIzVS9

Reflecting on Saturday’s defeat by Leeds in his programme notes, Glasner wrote: “I saw plenty of encouraging signs from the team on Saturday and I felt we were a lot closer to scoring than we were conceding, especially in the second half. Unfortunately, the small margins were not on our side.

The hosts’ kits tonight will include Carabao Cup sleeve patches with the number four on them, in recognition of the club’s League Cup triumphs in 1978, 1979, 1989 and 1990.

This is Forest and Leeds Part 2, just four days after they clashed in the Premier League.

Daniel Farke ruined the Oliver Glasner welcoming party on Saturday with a 1-0 smash-and-grab victory at the death.

The big breaking news is that Forest are smashing their club record to sign Chelsea forward Liam Delap for £45m.

Delap will undergo a medical at Forest on Wednesday with the deal potentially rising to £50m after add-ons.

It eclipses the previous transfer record of £37.5m for winger Omari Hutchinson.

Oliver Glasner has prioritised the addition of a new centre-forward this summer and Delap ticks pretty much every box for him.

Our @Carabao_Cup XI this evening. 📋 pic.twitter.com/Wv918WJScj

Welcome to live coverage of the Carabao Cup second-round match between Nottingham Forest and Leeds United. This will be the sides’ second meeting at the City Ground in four days after Anton Stach’s late free-kick decided an attritional contest on the Premier League’s opening weekend. Forest’s new head coach Oliver Glasner is something of a cup specialist, though, with FA Cup, Europa League and Conference League titles to his name and he will relish the opportunity to right the wrongs of Saturday in front of the Forest faithful.

The Austrian is Forest’s fifth head coach in less than 12 months and he will look to arrest the churn by bringing to the City Ground the success he enjoyed with Crystal Palace. During pre-season, the Austrian moulded Forest into his preferred 3-4-3 shape, placing summer acquisition Ousmane Diomande alongside the existing central-defensive partnership of Murillo and Nikola Milenković. Here, Diomande gets his Forest debut and Glasner brings in talisman Chris Wood from the start.

Daniel Farke will have been delighted to see his Leeds side continue their excellent form in pre-season – which included victories over Liverpool, Red Bull Leipzig and Augsburg – into the season proper. Although Leeds arrive at the City Ground shorn of attacking options Wilfried Gnonto, Noah Okafor and Mateo Joseph through injury, Farke still shuffles the pack in the forward positions with this weekend’s visit of Brentford to Elland Road in mind.

#2020. Savio scores on debut as Spurs cruise past Charlton in Carabao Cup

It looked like this was going to be a night for “one of their own”, but Tottenham Hotspur’s latest big-money arrival, Sávio, stole the headlines to crank up the excitement at his new club.

Mikey Moore had set Spurs on their way to what proved a comfortable Carabao Cup success over Championship club Charlton Athletic and heard his name sung by the home fans.

But Sávio stepped off the substitutes’ bench to take the limelight with a late goal just a few days after completing his expensive switch from Manchester City, and head coach Roberto De Zerbi is demanding many more to come.

“A perfect day for him,” said De Zerbi. “His biggest improvement is to increase the number of goals. He is one of the best wingers, but the best wingers score many goals and I spoke with him two days ago, and we put the goal at 10-12 goals.

“We need 10-12 goals from the wingers. Last season, we suffered too much because the number of goals were not enough.”

"What an introduction!"Sávio scores a brilliant goal on his Spurs debut! 👏 pic.twitter.com/WgmcfgeNpX

Having watched some of Tottenham’s signings fall to a 3-0 Premier League defeat by Brentford a few days earlier, Sávio’s late impact was the perfect lift for the Spurs supporters.

The club have committed to spending almost £400m this summer, leading to debate by outsiders over whether it will prove to be money well spent and huge waves of excitement within the fanbase.

A deal that could be worth as much as £85m, if add-ons are achieved, for Sávio certainly raised some eyebrows, but the Brazilian provided the perfect response by scoring just 11 minutes into his debut as a late substitute.

In the 82nd minute, Sávio cut in from the flank and scored with a shot past Charlton goalkeeper Tiernan Brooks. He and the Spurs crowd thought he had a second a few minutes later, but his shot hit Ben Davies on its way into the net and the defender was credited with the goal.

Having sung for Moore earlier in the game, the Spurs fans wasted no time in trying out their new song for Sávio, inspired by the Spandau Ballet hit Gold.

Moore has been expected to move to Cologne on loan, but provided a reminder of his talent by opening the scoring in the first half with only his second goal for the club.

What a hit from Mikey Moore! ⚪ pic.twitter.com/OgSM4qhiqs

“We have to understand the best solution,” De Zerbi said. “I would like to keep him. He’s young but a good player, but we can’t make the wrong decision. He needs to play, he needs to get games inside him.”

Cutting in from the right, where Sávio is primed to play, Moore surged past his marker and shot from just inside the box. Brooks should have stopped it, but the ball flew past him and into the net.

Three minutes after Moore’s opener, Dominic Solanke scored his first goal since March to offer a reminder of what he can still give De Zerbi, who is poised to welcome Omar Marmoush to Tottenham.

Buoyed by his first-half goal, Moore skipped his way around a couple of tackles at the start of the second period but his low cross was cut out. The Spurs fans responded by singing “he’s one of our own.”

Substitute Kevin Danso netted with his first touch from a header, before Sávio was introduced to steal the show, despite a late consolation goal from Charlton’s Lloyd Jones.

Kevin Danso scores with his first touch since coming on! ⚪ pic.twitter.com/oqUU7wjoJW

The victory set up a tough third-round trip to Anfield to face Liverpool for Tottenham, but De Zerbi said: “It’s a great game. If we want to win the competition we have to win the games.

“Sometimes in this competition, it can happen that you play against big teams. It’s a great challenge for the players, for me, for our clubs. We have to arrive ready to play in our style, with personality, ready to play a game following the work we are doing on the training ground.”

At least the travelling Charlton fans have something to cheer about even if their side are being dumped out of the League Cup. A corner from the left comes to the back post, where Jones rises highest to head it between Kinsky’s legs and into the Tottenham net.

Savio thinks he has his second in quick succession but it will go down as Davies’ goal. Savio’s shot was on target but it deflects off Davies and goes in for Tottenham’s fifth on the night.

The Brazilian signed just yesterday but he now has a first Tottenham goal to his name. He cuts inside from the right and drives across the face of the penalty area before firing at the near post, beating Brooks. Tottenham are cruising into the third round and their newest signing scores on his debut.

Change for Tottenham as Williams-Barnett replaces Tel.

Tel crosses from the left side of the box and picks out Savio, who attempts an audacious flick that does not come off.

West Brom were not back on level terms for long as Barnes has his second of the game and Newcastle lead 3-2 with under 10 minutes remaining.

Charlton have barely threatened the Tottenham goal tonight but that is a decent opportunity for Leaburn, who is played in down the right and forces Kinsky into a decent save.

Savio is straight into the action with good work down the right and squares it for Tel, whose shot is straight at Brooks.

Savio is on for his Tottenham debut and replaces Solanke. Savio only joined Tottenham yesterday but makes his first appearance for the club tonight.

Danso has hurt himself as there was a clash of heads as he met the delivery and receives treatment to his head.

Charlton are also making a triple change of their own.

Gray is found on the left side of the Charlton penalty area and he drives his shot towards goal, forcing Brooks into a decent save. Tottenham are pushing for that third goal.

A cross is sent in from the right and it comes to Tel, who volleys first time but it is a fairly routine save for Brooks in the Charlton goal.

Tottenham are starting to ramp up the pressure as they go in search of a third goal. As it stands, the only side that looks like scoring is Tottenham.

Plenty of cheers from the home fans as Savio is out to warm up. Will Roberto De Zerbi turn to the Brazilian and give him his debut tonight?

Tottenham looked rather lethargic for a lot of that first half but two goals in quick succession has Roberto De Zerbi’s side in control. As the players head off, the DJ pays homage to the late Dolly Parton by blasting out Nine to Five.

Apter is booked for cynically tripping up Udogie.

Tottenham are currently too slow in possession and are not moving the ball quickly enough, meaning it is easier for Charlton to defend.

A corner from the right ends up coming out to the edge of the box, where Tel takes it first time but his volley goes a long way wide. That moment sums up Tottenham’s evening thus far.

Solanke has a shot from the edge of the box blocked before Gray’s effort with the outside of his right foot is saved well by Brooks down to his left. That looked like it was creeping in so Brooks had to get a hand to that.

Charlton play the corner short and eventually the ball comes in. Asiimwe meets it and has a good chance from eight yards out but his header goes just wide. That was a decent chance for Charlton.

That probably sums up Tottenham’s night thus far. Davies pings a lovely diagonal ball out to Moore in space down Tottenham’s right. Moore waits for the overlapping run of Gray before playing the pass but Gray’s attempted cross from the right side of the box is terrible and goes behind for a goal kick. Roberto De Zerbi is quickly out of his seat!

Roberto De Zerbi was keen to see his side show a reaction to their defeat at Brentford on Saturday. Unsurprisingly, they are dominating possession but have not posed much of a threat going forward.

There has been a goal at St James’ Park and it is the visitors West Brom who have taken the lead over Newcastle. Price has scored directly from a free-kick and the Championship side lead.

Moore wins Tottenham a corner out on the right, which summer signing Fernandes will take. His delivery is headed away and the danger is gone.

Sichenje has now got back to his feet so he may have avoided a serious injury but we will see if he can continue. It looks like he will try to continue at least.

Play is halted as Charlton defender Sichenje looks to be in a lot of pain as he bangs the ground in frustration. It appears to be his left knee and the visitors may be forced into an early change.

Inside the opening minute, Solanke thinks he will have a chance on goal as the ball is played in behind but there is too much on it and the ball goes through to Brooks in the Charlton goal.

A place in the League Cup third round is at stake as Tottenham host Charlton in a London derby at the Tottenham Hotspur Stadium. The last competitive meeting between these sides came in the FA Cup back in January 2011, with Tottenham winning that game 3-0 at White Hart Lane. A then 19-year-old Andros Townsend made his debut that day and scored, with Jermain Defoe scoring a brace.

Tottenham’s Premier League campaign got off to the worst possible start as they lost 3-0 at Brentford last weekend. Tottenham have been very busy during this summer transfer window and that has continued this week. Savio (formerly Savinho) has arrived from Manchester City in a deal that could be worth £85m and the Brazilian could make his Tottenham debut tonight, having been registered in time.

“I think in attacking positions we need players capable one-on one, to create something, to create a chance to score,” Roberto De Zerbi said. “In terms of one-on-one, he [Savio] is one of the best players, especially since 2024. He can play on the right side, on the left side. I have known him from a long time, I spoke with him when he went to Manchester City. He is a big player for us.

“I do not know if I am the right man [to get the most out of Savio], but for sure he has to achieve. I think a player who is so good in one-on-one, so good at creating chances to score, to be complete, he has to score. If you analyse the other best wingers in the world, many of them, they score 10 to 15 goals per season. He has the qualities. Maybe his habits, he has to change habits, because he has to be focused on the assists, the one-on-one dribbling and also to score.”

Omar Marmoush is closing in on an initial loan deal from Manchester City but that move is not complete and thus he is not available for Tottenham tonight. Micky van der Ven and Pedro Porro are both available having missed Tottenham’s loss at Brentford but the hosts are still without Xavi Simons, Pape Sarr, Dejan Kulusevski and Wilson Odobert.

Charlton have made the perfect start to their Championship campaign; a 2-1 home win over Derby was followed up by a 2-1 victory at recently-relegated West Ham. Nathan Jones’ side earned their place in the League Cup second round with a 3-1 win at Cheltenham in the first round.

“We have to be very organised and very professional, they [Tottenham] are a top team,” Jones said. “They have a great manager and a brilliant group of players. They already had a Premier League squad and they have spent, what is reaching about, I do not know, £300 million or something like that. It is a wonderful test, we have to be right near our best and do both sides of the game very well. Of course, you want to test yourself against the best managers and you want to test yourself against the best teams. For us, this is not our priority, the Championship is our priority, but this is the next game and therefore it is the most important.”

#2019. Iraola will be beaming: Liverpool handed massive double injury boost ahead of Man United clash

Liverpool have been handed a significant double injury boost in the days leading up to their Premier League clash against Manchester United.

Andoni Iraola will be pleased that his players who were on international duty all seem set to return to Merseyside unscathed, even though Dominik Szoboszlai controversially played through the pain barrier for Hungary.

The Reds’ head coach is still waiting for a handful of long-term injury absentees to become available once more, but two of those have now taken a major step in their respective recoveries.

As reported by Paul Joyce for The Times, Conor Bradley and Giovanni Leoni have returned to Liverpool first-team training, with both defenders having been sidelined for a number of months with serious knee injuries.

The Northern Ireland right-back has been out of action since January after he was struck down towards the end of the 0-0 draw at Arsenal; while the Italian teenager has been absent for even longer, not playing since rupturing his ACL on his Reds debut in September 2025.

The latter had been due to resume full training in early October before that staging post was delayed as medical staff took a cautious approach, but he’s now in the final stages of his recovery to full fitness and could resume playing in the coming weeks.

Want more Empire of the Kop coverage? Add us as a preferred source on Google to your favourites list for news you can trust

While we wouldn’t bank on either of the Liverpool duo returning to matchday action in the concluding weeks of 2026, their resumption of first-team training comes as a huge step towards their long-awaited comebacks.

Bradley would very likely have made the right-back position his own this season had he not been sidelined, but thankfully Ronald Araujo has excelled in that role since joining on loan from Barcelona in August.

As for Leoni, it was beyond cruel that he tore his ACL towards the end of what had been a terrific Reds debut against Southampton 14 months ago, but he’s still only 19 and should hopefully have a hugely successful career still ahead of him.

Even when both players are cleared for a return to action, it’ll take time for them to properly get back into a matchday rhythm, and Iraola will surely bed them in gently after missing so much football over the past few months.

However, having them back in a full training feels like a significant step forward, and when the time comes for them to resume playing, it’ll be a wonderful sight for everyone associated with Liverpool.

#2018. Ian Wright praises ‘magnificent’ Ben White after England beat Spain

Ian Wright praised ‘magnificent’ Arsenal defender Ben White after England’s thrilling Nations League win over World Cup holders Spain.

England ended Spain’s incredible 43-match unbeaten run with a 3-2 victory in Madrid on Sunday evening.

The Three Lions were bright from the start and took the lead on the stroke of half-time through a penalty from England record goalscorer and Ballon d’Or winner Harry Kane.

Ezri Konsa headed in Declan Rice’s corner shortly after the interval and England were in dreamland when White added a third on the hour mark, arriving at the back-post and firing past Unai Simon.

Spain were being outplayed but had renewed hope when Elliot Anderson was sent off for bringing down Lamine Yamal as he raced through on goal and Mikel Oyarzabal converted the subsequent penalty.

Read exclusive analysis of the biggest stories in football with Metro's weekly football newsletter In The Mixer. Sign up now for free.

England fans were having flashbacks of last summer’s World Cup semi-final collapse against Argentina when Nico Williams scored Spain’s second to set up a tense final 20 minutes.

The hosts pressed for an equaliser but were denied by some valiant England defending and an impressive display from goalkeeper James Trafford.

The hard-fought win means England, already through to the quarter-finals of the Nations League, finish top of their group ahead of World Cup holders Spain.

Wright felt England ‘deserved’ the win despite the late pressure from Spain and singled out Arsenal star White for special praise.

Use AI to go deeper into the stories you care about – powered by Metro and trusted publications.

White was part of England’s World Cup group in Qatar four years ago but left Gareth Southgate’s squad for personal reasons.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video

He then made himself unavailable for selection for the rest of Southgate’s reign, a decision that has led to him being booed by some England fans in recent games.

‘Can I just say, I’m really pleased for Ben White and the way things have turned around for him,’ Wright said on ITV.

‘It’s just brilliant for him to get back in and he was magnificent tonight. Not just with the goal but he was making tackles, niggling the Spain players. I’m so pleased it’s ended that way for him.

"This England team are RUNNING RIOT in Spain" 🤩👀 They lead the World Cup winners by 3-0 in Madrid!! WOW. pic.twitter.com/2GuDnscRb4

‘There was a lot to be excited about for England. They were 3-0 up and cruising against the world champions before the red kind of changed the game.’

Meanwhile, Arsenal midfielder Rice said the England squad ‘knew’ they were going to end Spain’s two-year unbeaten run.

‘We knew we were going to beat them tonight,’ he said on ITV. ‘The message from the manager after the Croatia game has been so positive.

‘The first 10 minutes was the best we’ve played. Overall 10 men for half an hour, winning 3-2 against a team unbeaten in 43 is massive.

‘Argentina that day [at the World Cup] wasn’t meant to be. That’s football. When they [Spain] got a second maybe it could have gone another way. It’s a massive win.’

Transfer Correspondent AUTHORITY Former Sky Sports and ESPN FC correspondent who specialises in global recruitment, contract negotiations, and high-velocity transfer breaking news. FOCUS Exclusive reporting, domestic and international transfer markets, and elite-level insights. Dinamo Bucharest winger Danny Armstrong is keen to move to Rangers in January, sources have told Football Insider.

The 29-year-old has emerged as a target for Derek McInnes' side, after the wideman previously played under the Gers boss at Kilmarnock.

McInnes "knows all about" Armstrong as a player, and is understood to be hopeful of reuniting with him in the upcoming transfer windows.

Sources say that the player is also keen to return to Scotland, and would find the chance to move to Ibrox "hard to turn down" this winter.

Armstrong has been away from Scottish football since 2025, but has since been flourishing in Romania.

The forward has already notched six goals and 10 assists from just 15 gams for Dinamo this term, making him the most productive player in Romania's top flight.

Armstrong was already at Kilmarnock when McInnes first took the reins there back in January 2022, but he quickly became a key figure for the boss.

He starred in his team's surprise fourth-placed finish in the Premiership back in 2023-24, notching 16 league goal involvements along the way.

McInnes was a big fan of the wideman, who made 40 or more appearances in all competitions in each of his three campaigns in charge.

The pair both left Rugby Park in 2025, but only after they led them to within one game of a place in the league phase of the UEFA Conference League.

McInnes and Armstrong enjoyed a hugely successful relationship during their time together, and have since both gone on to new heights in their careers.

With both parties open to a deal in the coming months, it would be no surprise to see Armstrong return to Scotland with Rangers.

Former Aberdeen chief executive Keith Wyness recently told Football Insider that Vanja Dragojevic's recent struggles may be down to him "not settling" well in Glasgow.

The midfielder joined Rangers from Partizan Belgrade in the summer, but has been starved of game time over the last few months.

Wyness believes that moving to Glasgow may have been a big culture shock for the 20-year-old, and pointed out that several players have struggled to adapt over the years.

Dragojevic remains highly-rated at Rangers, but has played just seven minuts of football since the end of August.

#2016. Declan Rice says England ‘knew’ they would beat World Cup holders Spain

Declan Rice says the England squad ‘knew’ they would beat World Cup holders Spain in their final Nations League group game.

England earned top spot in their Nations League group and ended Spain’s extraordinary 43-game unbeaten run with a thrilling 3-2 win in Madrid.

Thomas Tuchel’s side scored three goals in 12 minutes either side of half-time to stun Spain before withstanding a late siege to seal their finest win under the German boss.

Harry Kane took his international tally to 93 goals with a penalty on the stroke of half-time as England deservedly ended the opening 45 minutes ahead.

Arsenal defenders Ezri Konsa and Ben White then scored twice in the space of four minutes to open up a commanding 3-0 lead over the shell-shocked Spaniards.

Read exclusive analysis of the biggest stories in football with Metro's weekly football newsletter In The Mixer. Sign up now for free.

But Elliot Anderson’s red card on 63 minutes and Mikel Oyarzabal’s subsequent penalty offered Spain a route back into a match they looked out of.

England fans feared a collapse similar to the one the team suffered in last summer’s World Cup semi-final against Argentina when Nico Williams scored Spain’s second with 20 minutes remaining.

But this time England kept their opponents at bay with some resolute defending and two superb saves from goalkeeper James Trafford.

Rice was full of praise for his teammates after the Nations League win and said he ‘knew’ England would beat the world champions in their own backyard.

Use AI to go deeper into the stories you care about – powered by Metro and trusted publications.

‘We knew we were going to beat them tonight,’ Rice told ITV. ‘The message from the manager after the Croatia game has been so positive.

"We knew we were going to beat them tonight!"Declan Rice after England's win over Spain in Madrid 🇪🇸🏴󠁧󠁢󠁥󠁮󠁧󠁿 pic.twitter.com/dbNiMi74od

‘Our first ten minutes were probably the best we’ve played. It was pressure, pressure, pressure – we could have had two or three.

‘If we don’t go down to ten men, we see more of the ball, we start to see them jump more, we start to see more space, and we start to see our attacking players thrive like they were doing in the second half.

‘With ten men for half an hour, winning 3-2 against that team is massive. It’s a massive win. Credit to everyone.

‘When they got the second, you might have thought that it was going to go the other way with the amount of pressure they were putting on, but that resilience.

‘Keep emptying the tank, doing anything for this badge, for this team, for our players, for the manager.’

Meanwhile, Tuchel hailed England’s ‘brilliant performance’ after they beat a side who last lost in regulation play in March 2024.

‘Brilliant performance. Well deserved win,’ he said. ‘Overall we were the better team. Fantastic performance from start to finish.

‘It was a long 30 minutes after the red card but I don’t want to focus on that. There were so many positive things in the first 60 minutes.

‘Complete performance. We brought everything to the table. We were brave. Spirit wise, energy wise and also football quality was highest level.

‘We deserved it. We focused on our performance and attitude. I can’t praise the team high enough for what they put out there.’

#2015. Luis de la Fuente singles out ‘fantastic’ England star after Spain defeat

Luis de la Fuente reserved special praise for James Trafford following Spain’s 3-2 defeat to England, hailing the goalkeeper’s ‘fantastic’ display in Madrid.

England produced arguably their finest all-round performance under Thomas Tuchel in Sunday’s Nations League classic to land a hefty psychological blow on the reigning world and European champions.

The Three Lions flew out of the blocks from minute one and were duly rewarded for their efforts as captain Harry Kane converted from the spot to break the deadlock on the stroke of half-time.

Goals from Arsenal defenders Ezri Konsa and Ben White increased the deficit after the restart, with Spain all at sea before Elliot Anderson’s sending off handed the hosts a lifeline.

Mikel Oyarzabal scored with the resulting penalty before Nico Williams finished off a flowing Spanish move to set up a tense final 15 minutes at Atletico Madrid’s Metropolitano Stadium.

Read exclusive analysis of the biggest stories in football with Metro's weekly football newsletter In The Mixer. Sign up now for free.

But ten-man England managed to keep La Roja at bay thanks largely to an inspired Trafford, who was selected over Jordan Pickford and repaid Tuchel’s faith with a series of stunning late stops to help preserve the visitors’ narrow advantage

Trafford’s double save to keep out Fermin Lopez and Aymeric Laporte earned the Leeds United keeper immediate high fives and adulation from his team-mates.

The result brought Spain’s incredible 43-match unbeaten streak to a halt and ensured England finished top of their Nations League group having picked up 15 from a possible 18 points.

‘Positives? There are a lot of positives to find here. It’s very difficult to get here, to achieve the numbers that we’ve achieved,’ Spain boss De La Fuente said when asked about Spain’s run being brought to an end.

Use AI to go deeper into the stories you care about – powered by Metro and trusted publications.

‘It’s something historical that we’ve done. We’ve been champions of the Nations League, the Euros, the World Cup, everything is positive.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video

‘But we know how to win and we know how to lose. And we have to say that we faced a rival that we managed to beat in the past but I have to say that they were the better team in the first 30 minutes.

‘I had a feeling we could get there when they went one man down but I’m really proud of this team, their hunger, their eagerness.

‘I’m convinced that the best is yet to come for this team.’

De la Fuente made four second-half substitutions as they looked to claw their way back into the contest, with Fermin Lopez, Nico Williams, Pedri and Dean Huijsen all sent on in the Spanish capital.

But the home team were thwarted by Trafford’s heroics in the closing stages – and De la Fuente took the opportunity to applaud the ‘keeper’s outstanding showing.

‘What we wanted to do with the substitutions was try to go all out, try to generate more chances,’ he explained.

‘We did generate some chances but England’s goalkeeper has produced a fantastic performance and stopped two or three potential goals in the last ten or 15 minutes.

‘In any case, there were many alternatives but again, I want to say how fantastic England were on the night.’

Asked what he and Tuchel had discussed shortly after the final whistle, De La Fuente replied: ‘We just spoke for a few seconds about what happened this week and we just wanted to clarify things.

‘I have no problem with him at all, all I have is admiration and respect.

‘As for the dressing room, when you are not used to losing, you look at eachother and ask, “What happened here?”, so what did I tell my players? I told them that we haven’t lost for three years and we’ve won all the important tournaments.

‘All I wanted to do was say how proud I am of them because of this and it’s a shame we don’t have another game coming up, we have to wait until March.’

The Spain head coach added: ‘We’ll surely come back in March with renewed energy, thinking about the Nations League final.

‘We’re going to try to get there, knowing difficult it is to get there and win a competition like this.

‘But the spirit, the intention, the ambition are all there.’

#2014. Mauricio Pochettino eyeing two USA players to bring to Man United - Transfer expert

Mauricio Pochettino could consider bringing Weston McKennie and Folarin Balogun to Manchester United with him.

That is according to experienced former Tottenham, Everton and Aston Villa scout, Bryan King, speaking exclusively to Football Insider.

The 54-year-old's appointment was confirmed last week, with his first game in charge to come against Liverpool at Anfield on Sunday.

Pochettino was in charge of the United States for two years and guided them to a positive World Cup campaign in the summer, earning himself a new contract that he signed in August.

But the Argentine could not turn down Man United's offer down, and will return to the Premier League with a third team after stints at Tottenham and Chelsea.

His first transfer window will be a key one, with the Red Devils in the relegation zone and in need of major intervention.

McKennie and Balogun have been key parts of Pochettino's US team in the past two years.

The former is a key player for Juventus and has been capped 72 times by his country, appearing on both wings and in the centre of the pitch.

Balogun, on the other hand, declared for the US in 2023 and has scored 13 goals in 32 caps since. The 25-year-old came very close to signing for Everton on transfer deadline day and is expected to leave Monaco.

"I bet he wishes he could take Harry Kane," King told Football Insider when asked what Pochettino could take from his experience with Tottenham.

"Pochettino was obviously involved when Harry broke into the team. Manchester United, like Tottenham, need a centre-forward. There's no chance of Harry Kane going there, that is for sure.

"He's got a couple of options with the American players. He's got the boy McKennie at Juventus. He's got the lad who's at Monaco, Balogun.

"He didn't win anything at Tottenham. He played decent football, but decent football doesn't wash at Manchester United. They've got to win cups."

Speaking last week, Pochettino was asked about potentially signing players from his squad with the US.

"Now is not the time [to talk about this]. All the good players always have dreams to reach the highest level," he said. "And I think Manchester United is one of the teams that is in the highest level and it's the dream for many of the players.

"But now, I think they need to be focused on today, on tomorrow's game, on their clubs. I know really well for more than two years every single player. And I think they are all players with unbelievable talent.

"Of course, in the future, when that happens, of course we are going to pay attention, you know, to make some decisions and to pay attention to players that we know really well."

#2013. Premier League KMI Panel unanimously admits to another refereeing error which wronged Liverpool

The Premier League’s Key Match Incidents (KMI) Panel has adjudged that Liverpool had a penalty wrongly given against them in a recent fixture.

The Reds won their last game before the international break, beating Crystal Palace 3-1 at Selhurst Park, although Alisson Becker was denied a clean sheet by a stoppage-time spot kick awarded to the home side and converted by Eddie Nketiah.

The penalty was awarded for what referee Tony Harrington deemed to be a foul by Milos Kerkez on Dario Osorio when the two players unfortunately clashed heads, and Andoni Iraola said afterwards that he was ‘very upset‘ over that decision.

The Premier League’s KMI Panel has now published its findings from the most recent top-flight matchday (via premierleague.com), and all five independent assessors adjudged that the penalty award against Liverpool was incorrect.

However, there was also unanimous agreement that VAR was right not to intervene, as it was decreed that no ‘clear and obvious’ error had taken place.

The panel concluded: ‘The panel unanimously felt that the referee’s call of a penalty for a challenge by Kerkez on Osorio was incorrect, with the contact being inevitable given the jumping actions of both players.

‘However, the non-intervention of VAR was supported on the basis it was not a clear and obvious error.’

Want more Empire of the Kop coverage? Add us as a preferred source on Google to your favourites list for news you can trust

Liverpool fans must be getting sick of hearing from the Premier League’s KMI Panel at this stage, with this incident coming fresh off the back of the panel ruling that we should’ve had a penalty for Jurrien Timber’s blatant shirt pull on Alexander Isak in the 0-1 defeat to Arsenal.

The incident with Kerkez and Osorio wasn’t as black-and-white, but the decision to award a spot kick still felt rather curious at the time. Luckily for Harrington, it came too late to have any major bearing on the overall result at Selhurst Park.

Still, to hear that an independent panel unanimously acknowledged that the Reds were wronged by another refereeing error is galling for everyone associated with LFC, and yet again it calls into question the standads of officiating in the Premier League.

It’s the kind of inconsistency between Kerkez having a spot kick given against him for a 50/50 duel, and Timber getting away with a blatant infringement, which drives players, coaches, fans and pundits absolutely berserk.

Thankfully the decision in the Palace game didn’t do any lasting harm for Liverpool, but you get the sense that it won’t be long before another contentious decision goes against us and the KPI Panel is wheeled out to tell us what we can already deduce for ourselves.
