#1957. Mary Fowler was offered a record $1million to return home and reunite with Nathan Cleary - but she said no

Published: 21:52 EST, 11 November 2026 | Updated: 21:57 EST, 11 November 2026

A reported record-breaking pay offer and the chance to live closer to Nathan Cleary were not enough to bring Mary Fowler back to Australia.

The Matildas star remains at Manchester City after a reported $1million offer emerged as part of an ambitious plan to recruit Australian sport’s glamour couple to two clubs under the same ownership umbrella.

The proposal could have offered a solution to the long-distance relationship that keeps their careers on opposite sides of the world.

For battling NRL franchise Wests Tigers, it was an extraordinary bid to prise one of rugby league’s biggest names away from Penrith.

According to News Corp, Tigers owner Holman Barnes Group proposed a combined package worth $9million, including a $1million marquee contract for Fowler to join the Central Coast Mariners women’s team.

The group had acquired the Mariners women’s side, opening the door to a recruitment pitch spanning two sports.

Mary Fowler remains at Manchester City despite a reported $1million offer to return to Australian football

A proposed recruitment package would have brought Fowler to the Central Coast Mariners and Cleary to Wests Tigers

Fowler returned to Australia in October to support Cleary following two operations

Under the reported proposal, Cleary would have joined the Tigers and Fowler would have returned to NSW on what would be the highest salary in A-League Women history.

But the blockbuster homecoming did not materialise.

Fowler, 23, is contracted to Manchester City until 2028, meaning any move would also require an agreement with the English club over her release.

She has built a formidable profile away from the pitch, with News Corp reporting that her multi-year Adidas deal is worth $10million.

Her other commercial work includes a L’Oréal Paris ambassadorship and Chobani’s national ‘Game Changer’ campaign.

The couple’s long-distance relationship attracted renewed attention in October when Fowler returned to Australia to support Cleary as he recovered from two operations.

She withdrew from Matildas friendlies against Germany and Haiti for personal reasons in October, prompting questions about her sudden absence.

Football Australia said the decision followed discussions between Fowler, Manchester City and Matildas staff.

Fowler’s commercial pulling power extends well beyond football, with  her multi-year Adidas deal worth $10million

Fowler became L’Oréal Paris’s first female athlete ambassador for Australia and New Zealand in 2024, adding a major beauty partnership to her growing profile

Fowler fronts Chobani’s national ‘Game Changer’ campaign, appearing across billboards, public transport and digital advertising as the brand launches its high-protein drinks

Should athletes choose love or loyalty to their teams when faced with life-changing offers?

Teammate Hayley Raso revealed the news had caught her by surprise.

‘I haven’t spoken to Mary. I only just found out the news myself,’ Raso said.

‘Obviously, Mary’s a really valuable player for our team, so it’s sad that she’s not here at this camp, but obviously, she has to take care of some personal circumstances.’

Cleary had fractured his fibula and dislocated his ankle during Penrith’s preliminary final loss to Newcastle, with a bone breaking through the skin.

He also had a fracture in his other foot.

Panthers chairman Greg Alexander later explained that the damage, while confronting, could have been worse.

‘The tibia didn’t break, no fracture in the tibia, which was fantastic news,’ Alexander told SEN.

‘In terms of the horrific injury that Nathan suffered, it was as good as could be expected without the double fracture.’

Cleary has since reportedly passed up another offer to remain with the club where he won four consecutive premierships.

The NRL expansion club the PNG Chiefs proposed a package worth up to $8.4million over three years, according to News Corp.

That reportedly included $6million in tax-free playing payments and a potential $2.4million in third-party endorsements.

Nine reported that Cleary told the Chiefs he intended to stay at Penrith, where he was expected to sign a two-year extension through to the end of 2029.

#1956. Celtic succession plan slammed as Dermot Desmond tipped to avoid December ‘chaos’ with digital move

Celtic’s board have been slammed for their lack of ambition and told it feels like they have “no plan” for when Martin O’Neill finally exits his role as manager.

Main shareholder Dermot Desmond and the board have faced several protests over the last 12 months, with the hierarchy at loggerheads with Celtic support over how the club is run, their perceived lack of footballing ambition and player recruitment.

Did you know with a Digital Subscription to The Scotsman, you can get unlimited access to the website including our premium content, as well as benefiting from fewer ads, loyalty rewards and much more.

Recently, ultras fan group The Green Brigade has announced a boycott of all Scottish Cup matches and home Europa League fixtures, and former Celtic winger Charlie Nicholas admits he is concerned for the Scottish champions’ future, with tensions building ahead of the club’s annual AGM next month.

“Dermot Desmond is doing everything he can to frustrate the hardcore fans by not spending any money,” said Nicholas, speaking on the No Tippy Tappy Football Podcast from Footy Accumulators and BOYLE Sports. “They’re in turmoil with supporters, and that’s not going to go away. There’s an AGM coming up on 1 December, which was chaotic last season. They had to abandon it, and I don’t know how they’re going to get around this.

“There’s talk it might go digital rather than in person. But they’ve got major overheads, and Martin and his staff are finding it difficult to overcome this, because a lot of supporters aren’t going. Our judgement of Celtic is always going to be about Europe. We’ve won one game, and we only just got through it at the tail end of the other week. It’s not been good. The standard at the moment is very disappointing, to say the least.”

Nicholas, who won every domestic honour with Celtic during two spells in his playing career, is also concerned about how the club will replace veteran manager O’Neill when he decides his time in the game is over. The 74-year-old signed a one-year contract with the option of a further year in the summer. However, Nicholas isn’t convinced the club has a plan in place for when the Irishman boss calls time on his management.

Former Celtic loanee Robbie Keane was strongly linked to the vacant role in the summer, but talks were shelved after backlash from fans who were angered by the 46-year-old’s decision to remain in charge of Israeli side Maccabi Tel Aviv during the outbreak of the nation’s war against Gaza in 2023, with a section of Celtic fans openly supporting Palestine in the conflict.

“There have been a few suggested replacements for Martin O’Neill,” said Nicholas. “The strong talk in the summer was that they went after Robbie Keane. The word was that he more or less had the job, and that he’s still sitting in the background. That leads me into the debate that will continue with some sections of the Celtic fans and the shareholders. Until they get round that, there doesn’t look to be any evidence of a plan.

“What’s the next step of the ladder? Are we ready for Martin when he leaves? No, I don’t think they are ready. I just don’t know if the major shareholder is really wholehearted about it. There’s no one at the football club taking that responsibility now, so we’re drifting along at the moment. That’s why I understand where the real Celtic fans’ frustration is.”

#1955. Scotland best and worst case Euro 2028 qualifying draw scenarios as seeding pots confirmed

Scotland's potential qualification opponents for Euro 2028 - a tournament they will co-host - have been finalised following the conclusion of the Nations League group stage.

Seeding pots for the Euro 2028 qualifying draw, which takes place in Belfast on Sunday, December 6, were based solely on the performance of each team in the Nations League across the 2026 campaign.

Did you know with a Digital Subscription to The Scotsman, you can get unlimited access to the website including our premium content, as well as benefiting from fewer ads, loyalty rewards and much more.

Sebastien Pocognoli's men have been placed in Pot 3 due to finishing third in Group B1 after taking seven points from a possible 18 in an underwhelming start to life under the Belgian head coach.

Scotland finished nine points behind group winners Switzerland, who put seven goals past them without reply over two matches, and four points behind runners-up Slovenia, who also won at Hampden after a goalless draw in Ljubjlana. North Macedonia, who Scotland defeated home and away, finished bottom of the group on zero points.

Attention now turns to the Euro 2028 qualifiers, which will feature six groups of four and six groups of five. The five-team groups will begin their qualification campaign in March 2027 while the groups of four will not start until September 2027.

If Scotland are drawn into a group of four they will face a 10-month wait for their next competitive fixture with friendlies required to fill the empty calendar for March and June next year.

However, Scotland are more likely to be drawn into a group of five due to Uefa tilting the odds in favour of teams who are not involved in any Nations League play-offs or quarter-finals in March.

This would see Scotland play eight qualifiers instead of six, kicking off in March with further games in June, September/October and November.

Scotland cannot be drawn in a group with their co-hosts England, Wales or Republic of Ireland. While Northern Ireland are no longer staging tournament matches after Casement Park was dropped from the bid, they retain a special status in the qualifying draw and will also be kept apart from the co-hosts.

Scotland will draw one team each from Pots 1, 2, and 4, plus one team from Pot 5 if placed into one of the six five-team groups.

Here are the confirmed seeding pots and possible opponents for Scotland:

Pot 1: Belgium, Croatia, Denmark, France, Germany, Greece, Italy, Netherlands, Norway, Portugal, Spain. (England excluded).

Pot 2: Austria, Bosnia and Herzegovina, Czech Republic, Hungary, Serbia, Slovenia, Sweden, Switzerland, Turkey. (Northern Ireland, Republic of Ireland, Wales excluded).

Pot 3: Albania, Georgia, Iceland, Israel, Kosovo, Montenegro, North Macedonia, Poland, Romania, Scotland, Slovakia, Ukraine.

Pot 4: Armenia, Belarus, Bulgaria, Cyprus, Estonia, Faroe Islands, Finland, Kazakhstan, Latvia, Luxembourg, Moldova, San Marino.

Pot 5: Andorra, Azerbaijan, Gibraltar, Liechtenstein, Lithuania, Malta.

A dream draw for Scotland would involve facing the lowest ranked nations from each pot. Such a group would involve Greece, Bosnia & Herzegovina, San Marino and Gibraltar.

Another more favourable draw would pair Scotland with Denmark, Czechia, Moldova and Liechtenstein.

The nightmare scenario for Scotland would be drawing the highest ranked nation from each pot, which would involve matches against Spain, Switzerland, Finland and Azerbaijan.

Another more difficult draw would involve Scotland facing France, Austria, Bulgaria and Lithuania.

To qualify automatically for Euro 2028 Scotland must finish as one of the 12 group winners or eight best runners-up. The other four group runners-up enter the play-offs.

There is, however, a potential safety net for Scotland with Uefa reserving two spots for co-hosts who do not achieve qualification on the pitch. Assuming England as pot one seeds qualify, Scotland will be competing with Wales and Republic of Ireland to get in through the back door.

If two co-hosts qualify on the pitch, then Scotland and the other co-host who fail to qualify would automatically take advantage of the safety net.

The only scenario where Scotland would fail to make it to Euro 2028 via the safety net is if three co-hosts fail to qualify and Scotland's qualification record is the worst of the trio.

Scotland are only guaranteed to play Euro 2028 matches at Hampden if they qualify the proper way. Using the safety net opens the door to potentially playing their matches elsewhere.

#1954. Ex-Scotland hero makes brutal Pocognoli admission and urges manager to follow ‘energetic’ blueprint

Scotland have been branded “boring” under new head coach Sebastien Pocognoli and urged to rip up their current game plan to get back on track.

Pocognoli, 39, has won just two of his first six games in charge of the national team, and came in for some scathing criticism in the wake of the 4-0 Nations League defeat to Switzerland on Monday night, with many supporters believing the manager is struggling to adapt his tactics to fit the strengths of the squad.

Did you know with a Digital Subscription to The Scotsman, you can get unlimited access to the website including our premium content, as well as benefiting from fewer ads, loyalty rewards and much more.

Former Scotland international Don Hutchison believes Pocognoli’s side have looked predictable under their new manager, and believes the squad must take inspiration from fellow home nation Northern Ireland, who achieved promotion to League A of the Nations League with a battling 1-1 draw away to Hungary on Tuesday night.

“Watching Scotland last night I was bored,” he wrote on his official X account. “Watching the same football I see a hundred times over. Northern Ireland are a good example of not over playing for the sake of it. Why can’t Scotland use a fighting, energy, ratting with “intensity”? Forget this ‘keep ball style’ - it doesn’t suit Scotland.”

Hutchison, who earned 26 caps for Scotland and is best remembered for scored the winning goal in a 1-0 European Championship playoff second-leg victory over England at Wembley in November 1999, thinks that the current national team are a shining example of what can be achieved when a team plays with more intensity.

“Yep that’s how you do it,” he said after Northern Ireland’s draw with Hungary in Budapest. “Bottle. Character. Heart. Fitness and desire. Well organised but with a willingness to run hard. Well played Northern Ireland. “[Scotland should] Try something different. Why do Scotland think they can ‘out football’ the opposition? We haven’t got enough players to make that work. Just go a bit longer and get the fans engaged in the game. [Scotland were playing] tippy tappy football last night.”

Despite some stinging criticism, Pocognoli defended his side’s performance in St Gallen, saying it had some of the “best moments” he’s seen from his team so far in his half-dozen games in charge. Speaking to the BBC, he said: “The score is heavy with the 4-0, but I don't think it's a reflection of the game, if I'm really honest and objective. We had some very good moments in the game, we started the game like we wanted, aggressive away from home. We could decide to be low on the pitch, but we did what we wanted to plan.

“We played a good first half, we created chances, we were dominant in some moments in the game, and we faced Switzerland with different shapes and adapted well from the first minute. We conceded the goal from maybe one of the first chances they had. We also created chances, but we missed it. It means we were not clinical in that moment in the box.”

#1953. When is the Euro 2028 qualifying draw, who could Scotland play and when does qualifying begin

Scotland will soon discover which opponents they will face as they look to qualify for the third consecutive European Championship under new head coach Sebastien Pocognoli.

Ending a 23-year exile from major tournaments by sealing a spot at Euro 2020 (played in 2021) under former manager Steve Clarke, they repeated the trick three years later, edging out Norway for a spot in the 2024 tournament in Germany.

Now under new boss Pocognoli, a disappointing third-placed finish in the Nations League has made Scotland’s hopes of qualifying for Euro 2028 - a tournament they will co-host - slightly harder after results meant they were placed in Pot 3 of the draw.

Want to know when the draw will take place, how to watch and which teams Scotland could face and which they will avoid? Here is everything you need to know about the Euro 2028 qualifying draw:

The qualifying draw for the European Championships in 2028 will take place in Belfast, Northern Ireland, on Sunday 6 December 2026. The tournament will be co-hosted by the United Kingdom and Republic of Ireland.

If you want to stream the draw via your smart TV, laptop, tablet or mobile phone, the entire ceremony will be streamed for free via UEFA.tv and via the official UEFA YouTube channel.

Scotland’s third-placed finish in Nations League Group B1 means they will be placed into Pot 3 of the draw next month. They will be drawn against once team each from Pots 1, 2 and 4 and potentially pot 5, depending on if they are placed into one of the six five-team groups.

They can’t be drawn against England, Northern Ireland, Republic of Ireland or Wales, with UEFA keeping the tournament co-hosts separated in the qualifying phase of Euro 2028.

Pot 1: Belgium, Croatia, Denmark, France, Germany, Greece, Italy, Netherlands, Norway, Portugal, Spain.

Pot 2: Austria, Bosnia and Herzegovina, Czech Republic, Hungary, Serbia, Slovenia, Sweden, Switzerland, Turkiye.

Pot 3: Albania, Georgia, Iceland, Israel, Kosovo, Montenegro, North Macedonia, Poland, Romania, Scotland, Slovakia, Ukraine.

Pot 4: Armenia, Belarus, Bulgaria, Cyprus, Estonia, Faroe Islands, Finland, Kazakhstan, Latvia, Luxembourg, Moldova, San Marino.

The Euro 2028 qualifiers begin in March 2027, but Scotland’s campaign will depend entirely on the outcome of the qualifying draw in December.

As attested to above, Scotland will be placed into either a four-team or five-team group. If they are drawn in a four team group, fixtures will begin in March 2027. However, should they be drawn in a five team group, their first Euro 2028 qualifying fixture will take place in September 2027.

#1952. How Michael Carrick's Man United fell apart: Players' bust-up on flight back from Madrid, weakness in training and on touchline - and why dressing-room sources believe divided board 'hung him out to dry'

By CHRIS WHEELER, NORTHERN SPORTS WRITER and NATHAN SALT - FOOTBALL REPORTER

Published: 10:30 EST, 11 November 2026 | Updated: 06:44 EST, 12 November 2026

For the last two days, Michael Carrick has followed his familiar route towards Manchester United’s training base, nudging his black Land Rover past the security barrier at Carrington before 8am, and making his way into work just as he has for much of the last two decades as a player, coach and head coach at the club.

While Carrick's fate has been decided by men in suits in Monaco and Manchester, he has put on his training gear and gone through the motions of coaching whichever players are left during the international break.

It has become increasingly apparent that Carrick was a dead man walking in the two weeks since the United board gave him a stay of execution and bought themselves time after the 3-0 defeat by Bournemouth last month.

Having effectively been brought in as a caretaker when United plucked him off the beach in Barbados in mid-January, he left much the same way: merely keeping the seat warm for Mauricio Pochettino in the chaotic days that have led to his sacking.

Sources close to the United dressing room believe Carrick has been ‘hung out to dry’ as United dithered over his future and then began a futile attempt to appoint Pochettino as his replacement in secret.

This is the story of how Carrick's United fell apart. It is the story of how disgruntled players aired their dirty laundry in public and clashed in private. It is the story of how the club's boardroom became the backdrop for an executive power struggle. And it is the story of how the magic touch that saw Carrick land the job permanently just five months ago deserted him...

Michael Carrick is out as Manchester United manager - just ten league games after guiding United to third and being handed a two-year contract

Carrick has had to turn up as normal at Carrington this week even as the world knew he was for the chop. Some dressing-room sources say he has been 'hung out to dry'

Carrick would have seen the writing on the wall when he got up to give an impressive speech at a dinner in the Heritage Suite at Old Trafford on Friday night to celebrate the 40th anniversary of Sir Alex Ferguson’s appointment.

The significance of the occasion was not lost on Carrick. Ferguson was brought in to succeed Ron Atkinson on the same date in November 1986 with United one place above the relegation zone. Having boxed himself into an identical corner, Carrick too was on borrowed time.

Two days later, he stood helplessly on the touchline at Old Trafford as United played out a ridiculous 4-4 draw with Aston Villa. Twice his team fought back from two goals down, but it was the final proof for United bosses that change was unavoidable.

The biggest club in English football having to endure the humiliation of at least two weeks in the relegation zone was too much for them to stomach.

His body language after the Bournemouth game when a tearful and crestfallen Carrick offered what looked like a farewell wave to the Stretford End – four days after he approached fans in Como to apologise for an equally painful 4-1 Champions League surrender – suggested he was already done.

The 45-year-old limped on to another defeat at Chelsea, then presided over a barmy 3-2 comeback win over Roma and the bonkers draw with Villa. A consummate and composed midfielder for United, Carrick of all people knew this wasn’t the way football should be played.

All the while, he spoke like a man who could turn things around. They always do. But the performances and results told a different story.

His critics would argue that someone whose only previous job in management was at Middlesbrough should never have been put in charge of United in the first place.

Others would say the bravest move by the club would have been to thank Carrick for his admirable efforts in securing third place and Champions League qualification last season, and move on in the summer when Pochettino would have been available for free before signing a new contract as US coach with a £7million release clause.

Matheus Cunha's late winner sealed a remarkable comeback win over Roma last week - but it promised to be a false dawn for Carrick

The 45-year-old's body language after an earlier loss to Bournemouth had suggested he was done back then, with Carrick appearing to wave farewell to the Stretford End

Instead, Carrick was rewarded with a two-year deal in May and the wheels fell off in spectacular fashion. Rather like his friend and former team-mate Ole Gunnar Solskjaer, the honeymoon period gave way to something altogether less appealing.

At least Solskjaer stuck around for three more years. Having beaten the Norwegian to the job in January, Carrick’s reign lasted less than 10 months.

The similarities between the two men are striking. Ex-players who basked in the glory days under Ferguson and know what it takes to succeed at Old Trafford, but were incapable of lifting the modern-day Manchester United to similar heights.

Having replaced Ruben Amorim and inspired a remarkable turnaround in the second half of last season, Carrick must have thought he had a chance.

His calm demeanour and experience of life in the Old Trafford pressure cooker that had played a part in his appointment was in contrast to the emotional incontinence of Amorim. How strange then that it has given way to such calamity and chaos.

United got off to the worst possible start by losing at newly-promoted Hull City in August. Tigers boss Sergej Jakirovic belittled them by saying his goalkeeper Konstantinos Tzolakis might as well have been sipping a cup of tea, and the hits have just kept on coming for Carrick.

Aside from Bournemouth, there were the late equalisers scored by Ainsley Maitland-Niles and Dominic Solanke for Everton and Tottenham, the controversial winner conceded to 10-man Manchester City, crashing out of the Carabao Cup to Brighton after giving up a two-goal lead, and the defeats in Europe by Atletico Madrid and Como after going behind in the opening seconds.

By the time Alysson scored in the first minute for Villa on Sunday, United’s defence had become as leaky as the Old Trafford roof. The four goals Carrick’s side conceded took it to 15 in his final four games.

United's defence has been leaky all season long, with Ainsley Maitland-Niles' stoppage-time equaliser at Hill Dickinson Stadium among the goals to cost them valuable points

By the time Alysson scored in the first minute for Aston Villa on Sunday, United’s defence had become as leaky as the Old Trafford roof. They let in 15 in his final four games

So why the alarming decline from last season? The United players haven’t looked sharp after a disjointed World Cup summer that involved a more relaxed one-week training camp in Ireland. There have been too many injuries.

Some players have spoken of a drop-off in training under Carrick and his backroom staff. Others feel that the switch to a more possession-based 4-2-4 system was asking too much of a group who aren’t suited to it.

There was surprise that a man so invested in the club's academy used so few young players. Harry Amass was left kicking his heels despite the chronic shortage of left backs, JJ Gabriel's shock exit was an unwelcome distraction, and Shea Lacey's re-emergence came too late.

It would be grossly unfair to pin this all on Carrick though. He is just the latest unfortunate to pay the price for the shambles at United which runs from the boardroom to the dressing room.

Amid ongoing uncertainty over his future, there has been a power struggle behind the scenes between director of football Jason Wilcox and director of recruitment Christopher Vivell over who to replace him, while sources close to the Glazer family have revealed a growing dissatisfaction at how minority owner Sir Jim Ratcliffe and Ineos are running the club.

United failed Carrick in the transfer market last summer with a futile pursuit of his No 1 midfield target Elliot Anderson, and instead delivered Youri Tielemans and Andrey Santos.

Carrick could see trouble on the horizon when he spoke to the media at Carton House in Maynooth during that pre-season camp in early August, but tried not to rock the boat.

It was the day his daughter Louise was getting her A-level results. ‘You know, we would like more, we need to keep pushing for more,’ he said, using the word ‘push’ another nine times.

There has been a power struggle behind the scenes between director of football Jason Wilcox (centre) and director of recruitment Christopher Vivell (left) over who to replace Carrick

Some players have spoken of a drop-off in training under Carrick and his backroom staff

Carlos Baleba followed but an ankle injury meant that he couldn’t play until October, and the £70m signing then suffered a hamstring injury.

United blundered catastrophically by focusing on midfield and delaying improvements to other areas of the team until next summer. In particular, the decision not to sign cover for Luke Shaw and Benjamin Sesko backfired spectacularly as both players succumbed to injury.

Lisandro Martinez called out United’s underwhelming recruitment in Madrid by saying he expected more of Wilcox, and he isn’t the only one who feels that way.

Tielemans gave a terse ‘no comment’ when he was asked on camera about his team-mate’s remarks, but it’s understood the two players clashed on the team flight back to Manchester as cracks began to show in an increasingly unhappy camp.

The camaraderie fostered by rounds of golf involving Carrick and the players during the break in Ireland was beginning to fall apart.

It came to a head when captain Bruno Fernandes became the second member of the leadership group to speak out of turn, questioning Carrick’s tactics after the loss to Como.

Having continuously defended his players in the face of criticism from some of his former United team-mates over their lack of effort, Carrick’s spiky response that ‘if you don't run forward and you don't run back, you aren’t going to win’ perhaps revealed his true feelings about this group.

He and Fernandes settled their differences in a clear-the-air meeting, but the questions didn’t go away. When he was asked about their relationship again at the end of what proved to be his final pre-match press conference last Friday, Carrick tapped his inquisitor on the shoulder as he left the room at Carrington and said with a smile: ‘Nice try!’

It was typical of Carrick, who often met questions with the knowing grin of a man who couldn’t say what he really thought.

Lisandro Martinez and Youri Tielemans clashed on United's flight back to Manchester following the former's incendiary comments after a loss to Atletico Madrid

One issue has been Carrick’s rather passionless appearance on the touchline. ‘He doesn't upset anyone, but doesn't inspire anyone either,’ remarked one dressing room source

It got to the point where he was encouraged by the club to be a little more forthcoming in press conferences. There have been some barbed post-match exchanges in TV interviews with Sky Sports and Viaplay this season, and the five-minute monologue before the Bournemouth game was pure theatre.

But on the whole, Carrick’s ability to play a straight bat in front of the cameras was a welcome change for the Old Trafford hierarchy compared to the loose-lipped Amorim – particularly with the Amazon Prime documentary-makers following their every move.

‘He talks a lot but doesn't say much,’ said Roy Keane, never Carrick’s biggest fan, on Sunday. ‘I don't know if that's a tactic, like a politician.’

More of an issue was Carrick’s rather passionless appearance on the touchline, which seemed to be reflected in his team at times.

Always dressed in black, a hand placed studiously on his chin, it has contrasted with more animated adversaries such as Unai Emery, Roberto De Zerbi and Diego Simeone in recent weeks.

‘He doesn't upset anyone, but doesn't inspire anyone either,’ remarked one dressing room source.

The fans were always behind him though, even the ones who may have accepted some time ago that a change was needed. Support and sympathy were never in short supply for a coach who has been let down by the men in the directors’ box and the players on the pitch.

That much has been abundantly clear by the abuse meted out to Ratcliffe and Co this season, and the unprecedented scenes when the fans turned on the players after Bournemouth.

Carrick looks set to be replaced by former Tottenham and Chelsea boss Mauricio Pochettino (right)

Carrick has been known to stand alongside them in the past, and it would be no surprise to see him there again in future.

‘Oh, it’s Carrick you know…’ echoed his tribute song from the Stretford End as he disappeared down the tunnel for the last time on Sunday evening.

So another bites the dust. A good man. A United man. The right man for the job? Maybe not, as it turns out. That poisoned chalice now passes to Mauricio Pochettino.

#1950. Jurgen Klopp loves him but Brajan Gruda may never play for Brighton again

Brajan Gruda arrived at Brighton in 2024 as one of Europe's hottest prospects.

Albion paid around £25m to Mainz for the German playmaker as he joined on a four-year contract.

Did you know with an ad-lite subscription to SussexWorld, you get 70% fewer ads while viewing the news that matters to you.

"I saw the big impact he made in the Bundesliga and he's a player I admire a lot," said Brighton’s German head coach Fabian Hurzeler at the time.

Hurzeler also admired Gruda's style of play and describe the then 20-year-old as a "street footballer."

Jurgen Klopp used the same "street baller" term this week as Gruda - now 22 - made an impressive start to his senior Germany career.

He netted a fine individual goal on his full debut against Serbia last week and then grabbed a goal and two assists as Germany walloped the Netherlands 5-0 last night. Brighton's Bart Verbruggen was in goal for the Dutch.

After Gruda's excellent debut against Serbia, Klopp said he felt sorry for their left back Petar Sukacev. "That left-back, he's a poor lad!" said the former Liverpool boss Klopp.

Opta statistics backed up Klopp’s claim as they stated nine of Gruda's 14 dribbles against Serbia were successful.

"He's a fantastic player who loves to take people on and hasn't yet fulfilled his potential. He doesn't need to at his age, but he's shown an awful lot of positive signs," Klopp said.

So will he play for Brighton again and why did the Seagulls loan him out? Gruda made 45 appearances for Albion under Hurzeler in all competitions and showed glimpses of his potential with four goals and eight assists.

Niggling injuries and the fitness demands of the Premier League saw Gruda struggle to make a sustained impact. At times he featured in the No 10 role but largely he was behind the powerful Yankuba Minteh for the right wing slot.

Minteh joined for £30m in the same window as Gruda but the Gambian adapted faster. Gruda made just eight Premier League starts in the 2025-26 season and a change of environment was deemed beneficial by all parties and he joined RB Leipzig on loan for the second half of last campaign

“Brajan wants regular football, and we are not able to guarantee him that in the second half of the season," said Hurzeler.

Three goals and three assists for Leipzig in the Bundesliga convinced them to extend the loan for another season and Brighton were happy to sanction another temporary deal.

Sporting director Mike Cave said, “Brajan had a good second half of the season with Leipzig and was keen to explore the opportunity of remaining there for the coming year.

“This is a move that allows Brajan to continue to secure regular playing time at a good level, in an environment he knows well.”

Brighton are pretty sharp on their loan agreements but no doubt they will now be double checking the small print of the loan contract.

Leipzig are believed to have an obligation to buy at the end of the season, albeit with certain conditions - but the size of any potential transfer fee remains unclear.

His value is clearly going upwards and the loan agreement will likely allow Brighton to cash in, should they decide to sell. Further high-profile displays for Klopp's Germany will see that increase.

Gruda remains contracted with Albion until 2028 and this week Bayern Munich and Bayer Leverkusen were also credited with interest.

Transfer expert Florian Plettenberg posted: “The obligation to buy for Brajan Gruda will be activated in 2027 due to accounting reasons. The total package for RB Leipzig will amount to €30m, including bonuses. Gruda will then get a contract until 2031, which has already been agreed.

“Bayern have always had him on their list, even before his move to Brighton. However, he is currently not a concrete transfer target for Bayern – unless something extraordinary happens, such as the sale of Michael Olise.”

Gruda seems to prefer living and playing his football in Germany and whether he even considers moving back to Brighton remains to be seen. The Seagulls - who are flying high in the Premier League - also have a number of options on the right flank.

Minteh - who almost joined Liverpool last summer - is just returning from injury, while Paraguayan international Diego Gomez has also excelled in the wide right position this term.

Zadok Yohanna, Femi Azeez, Malick Yalcouye are all available, while the likes of Amario Cozier-Duberry and Harry Howell are out on loan.

Gruda's form is impressive but whether he returns to the Premier League with Brighton anytime soon is debatable. Attention will now likely turn to maximising their fee.

#1945. Peter Schmeichel fumes at Man United for 'very disrespectful' treatment of Michael Carrick as Mauricio Pochettino closes in on Old Trafford job - with club legend put out of his misery on Thursday

Published: 15:20 EST, 11 November 2026 | Updated: 06:48 EST, 12 November 2026

Peter Schmeichel has hit out at the 'very disrespectful' way that he believes beleaguered Manchester United manager Michael Carrick is being treated as he awaits his sacking at Old Trafford.

The former club captain has endured a torrid start to the season, and while the Man United hierarchy publicly backed him as recently as three weeks ago, Carrick is now set to be handed his marching orders following a crisis summit in Monaco.

Man United chief executive Omar Berrada and director of football Jason Wilcox flew to the Principality to meet with co-owner Sir Jim Ratcliffe to ratify the decision to move on from Carrick, with current USA head coach Mauricio Pochettino set to be appointed in his wake.

But with Carrick still taking team training at Carrington while plans for his ejection from the club made global headlines, Schmeichel admitted he felt deep sympathy for the former midfielder's awkward position.

'I think the way this is playing out is very disrespectful to him,' Schmeichel said on The Overlap Daily. 'If I’m honest, I don’t think he’s doing anything wrong.

Michael Carrick remains in limbo at Manchester United after a shocking start to the season

Omar Berrada and Jason Wilcox have been in Monaco discussing his dismissal this week

'I know the team that he’s in charge of is where they are in the table, but I don’t put all of that on him. There are so many things that have been going on at Manchester United literally since Alex (Ferguson) and (former chief executive) David Gill left the club. And it’s never been corrected.

'It’s not been the correct people, not the right people in charge, and slowly it’s just gone worse.'

Man United sit within the relegation zone as this international break plays out, with Carrick's men winless in the Premier League since late August.

Last-minute comebacks against Roma in the Champions League and Aston Villa in domestic action however may have briefly boosted morale at Old Trafford.

But to Schmeichel, the issue lies at the feet of those who recruit at the club, rather than Carrick himself.

'If you think about this transfer window now, it’s abundantly clear to everyone - everyone who knows just a little bit about football - that Manchester United needed defenders,' he continued. 'They got through a whole transfer window without signing a single defender.

'There was a little bit of talk about Lewis Hall joining the club or going for Lewis Hall. That didn’t happen. And so, they bought three midfield players. And we know, because we’ve been in the game for so many years, that you can’t win games - if you concede 30 goals in 10 games, then there is a problem, and that was not addressed.

'Now, was Michael Carrick in on those decisions? Well, it took them forever, forever, to give him the job. So, I suspect he wasn’t in any of those discussions about who to sign up until the point he got named as manager.

Former Man United goalkeeper Peter Schmeichel believes the club's treatment of Carrick has been demeaning

The under-fire manager turned up to take training for a second day in a row as speculation swirled over his future

'So yes, I do feel a lot of sympathy for Michael. I think what is happening is wrong. I think we should stick with Michael. I think we should just try and steady the ship a little bit and then get into January and then sign the players that he feels he needs to bring the team forward and then be realistic about what this season is all about. Obviously, it’s about climbing as high as Manchester United can in the table.'

By contrast, Schmeichel's co-pundit Tim Sherwood said he did not feel sorry for Carrick, because he will have understood the brutal situation he was stepping into at Man United.

The former Middlesbrough head coach served as interim manager for the second-half of the previous season following the sacking of Ruben Amorim, and was named on a permanent basis over the summer.

But while Schmeichel admitted that the life cycle of a Premier League coach was undeniably short, his issue is with the manner of treatment Carrick has received in the process of the changing of the guard in the dugout.

'If they’re looking for somebody else, then relieve the man of his duties,' the former goalkeeper argued. 'Don’t let him come into training yesterday. He took training yesterday. How disrespectful is that?

'How do you think this fella – I mean, he’s a human being. He’s a very, very good human being. He’s one of the nicest people you’ll ever meet in your life, and obviously you two know him well. So, treat the guy with respect. Tell him, "Sorry, mate. We don’t think that you are the future here. Here’s a cheque. Move on." But they’re not doing that. They’re dragging it out.'

Schmeichel was incensed too by Carrick's status within the club, wondering aloud whether, since they had taken 'weeks and weeks' to come to their messy, public decision, the club's hierarchy might not really understand what it is to truly represent the club.

'Do you think these people know? Do you think they care?' Schmeichel continued. 'These people are not Manchester United people.

'They don’t understand what it’s like to be one of the Manchester United people. They don’t know that. This is obviously part of the broader issue here, part of the reason the club is where they are now. I’m not saying I feel sorry for Michael, but I’m a little bit angry at how this great football club is treating one of its greatest players. Simple as that.'

Talks have been planned with Pochettino overnight on Wednesday, with the club's hierarchy thought to be preparing to dismiss Carrick face-to-face on Thursday.

Mauricio Pochettino remains locked in talks to take over at Old Trafford as the club's preferred candidate for the role

Pochettino is currently at the US Soccer base outside Atlanta preparing for a CONCACAF Nations League quarter-final double header against Haiti, and is due to speak to the media on Friday.

It’s unclear if he will remain in charge for those games. It is possible he could stay for the first leg in Kingston, Jamaica at the weekend and then travel to Manchester.

The second leg in Cincinnati is not until the early hours of Thursday, and it seems inconceivable that Pochettino would only take over at United on Friday with a huge game against Liverpool at Anfield 48 hours later.

It’s understood that the US Soccer Federation are ready for this contingency and have a succession plan in place should he leave.

It will cost Pochettino around £7million to buy himself out of his contract with the US Soccer Federation, with United ready to foot the bill.

The cost of bringing in his back-room team, including trusted assistants Jesus Perez and Miguel D’Agostino, will take the cost above £10m.

Meanwhile in Manchester, Carrick took training for the second day in a row at the club's Carrington training ground on Wednesday, arriving at 7.45am and departing shortly after 1.30pm.

Carrick has overseen the club's worst start to the season in 40 years, but the man himself remained adamant that he would not be falling on his sword after battling back to claim a draw against Villa.

In an awkward interview with Sky Sports' Patrick Davison, Carrick remained steadfast in the face of questions as to whether he would quit his role amid the turbulence.

'You know the situation, we haven't won enough games,' he said. 'But I expect to move forward with things we've been working on, showing a lot of the good from today tighten up a few mistakes and win some football matches.'

The 26-year-old has found himself behind Gabriel Gudmundsson in the left wing-back department but made an impressive appearance from the bench in Leeds’ 1-0 win over Tottenham Hotspur before the international break.

Former Manchester United and Southampton midfielder Schneiderlin, who played with Bard at Nice, has compared him to Red Devils star Luke Shaw.

He told ComeOn: “I played with Melvin Bard at Nice and saw his development first-hand. When he first arrived, he was already a good player. I compare his progression a bit to Luke Shaw.

“He put in a lot of work on his conditioning and physique during his early time at Nice. He did the work, and now he is much fitter.

“He's very difficult to beat one-v-one, possesses great stamina, and has a very good left foot. Ultimately, whether to stay will be his choice, but he's a quality player and I'm certain he still has plenty of room to improve even further.”

Gudmundsson has established himself among Daniel Farke’s most trusted lieutenants since his arrival in the summer of 2025 and could prove difficult to dislodge.

Bard, however, will have his sights set on a more prominent role heading towards the end of the calendar year.

After putting pen to paper at Elland Road in the summer, Bard said: “Playing in the Premier League has always been a dream of mine, ever since I was a child.

“Leeds is a historic club in the Premier League so it was an easy choice. Leeds has a great history which makes the club an attractive one.

#1941. ‘Back in Leeds’ - Leeds United’s forgotten man Mateo Joseph ‘focused on comeback’ as he shares update

Leeds United forward Mateo Joseph has declared he is “focused on the comeback” as he plots a return to the pitch.

The 23-year-old succumbed to an anterior cruciate ligament (ACL) injury in March, while out on loan at Mallorca in La Liga.

Did you know with a Digital subscription to Yorkshire Post, you can get access to all of our premium content, as well as benefiting from fewer ads, loyalty rewards and much more.

He had requested a move away from Elland Road in the previous summer and scored two goals across 30 outings in Spain before being sidelined.

Joseph is now back on British shores, rehabilitating with the help of specialists at Leeds.

Posting on Instagram, the former Spain and England youth international said: “Back in Leeds, focused on the comeback.

“Every day brings progress, every step takes me closer, things are looking up and we’re moving in the right direction. One step at a time.”

It is hard to envisage Joseph carving out a future at Leeds given the progress made by the club since his loan departure.

Whites boss Daniel Farke does not boast a wealth of forward options, yet Joseph would arguably find it tough to leapfrog Dominic Calvert-Lewin and Lukas Nmecha in the pecking order.

Speaking to The Yorkshire Post in the summer, Leeds icon Jermaine Beckford said: “Mateo has got talent. He's got technical ability. He's got good pace about him as well. We've seen when he's been with the under-21s how good he is at finishing.

“He's had a couple of decent goals as well for the first team, I remember the Chelsea game at Stamford Bridge. He's got it, he just needs to knuckle down, get rid of the external noise, focus on working his socks off, and I think he could [force his way back in].

“Do I think Daniel Farke and the hierarchy want to keep him knowing that he could possibly upset the apple cart? I'm not entirely sure. But it's for Mateo to come back and show that this is a new and improved version of himself. He's got the ability.”

#1940. Chelsea are great entertainers but possess clear weakness

Chelsea are promising to be this season’s Premier League entertainers and yet manager Xabi Alonso seemingly believes less is more when it comes to possession.

Alonso has started with two wins from two league games in charge of Chelsea, with his team scoring seven goals and conceding five. So far, it has been a lot of fun – if not entirely convincing.

But perhaps the most significant numbers are around how much – or how little – Chelsea are having the ball. Having finished their 3-2 victory over Fulham with 38.11 per cent of possession, Chelsea had just 25.6 per cent in the 4-3 success over Brighton and Hove Albion and successfully completed 146 passes. Both were their lowest figures on record in the Premier League.

“The data is not important,” Alonso said. “It’s how you play and what we can do better. I don’t say ‘today we need to have 60 per cent or 20 per cent’. I never talk about those things. It’s about how to prepare, how to be more competitive.”

Chelsea’s third goal against Brighton, scored in the 32nd minute, best summed up the London club under Alonso to date. It took the home side three passes to go from the edge of their own penalty area to João Pedro scoring against his former club.

Jorrel Hato passed the ball to Morgan Rogers, he then released Hato down the left and the wing-back slid the ball across for João Pedro to finish. It was a devastating counter-attack and should have put Chelsea on course for a much easier win.

Joao Pedro finishes off a deadly Chelsea counter-attack and gives the Blues a 3-0 lead 🔥 pic.twitter.com/wAr0ckIgXJ

“After 30 minutes, we are 3-0 and probably, in that moment, we have played too much the result,” Alonso said. “It’s quite normal, it happens in many teams. I am sure in the future we can manage it better.”

It is one thing outscoring Fulham and a depleted Brighton team without having the ball, but can Chelsea do that against the bigger and better teams? We will get an early indicator in the next game against Arsenal at the Emirates.

Alonso’s approach has some similarities to the way in which Antonio Conte set up his Chelsea title-winning team. Just as Conte converted Victor Moses into an effective right wing-back, Alonso started Pedro Neto there on Sunday.

After Roméo Lavia had opened the scoring, it was Neto who grabbed Chelsea’s second goal against Brighton by drifting into the penalty area to finish from Rogers’s low cross.

"It's a nightmare for the goalkeeper!"Bart Verbruggen and Mats Wieffer's collision leads to Romeo Lavia scoring his first goal for Chelsea ⚽️ pic.twitter.com/q5awbdwVV0

"Pedro Neto Pounces!"Morgan Rogers goes past his defender before sliding the ball across to Neto! 💥 pic.twitter.com/WHZCIGsOLl

But whereas Conte’s team gave up little at the back, Alonso’s Chelsea are yet to balance their effective transitional play with shutting out their opponents.

Neto was partly to blame for Brighton’s first goal, as he missed a challenge in the build-up to Malick Yalcouyé’s brilliant volley. Making his Chelsea debut, goalkeeper Emiliano Martínez could do nothing to stop it and can expect to be kept busy this season if things do not change.

“I have come here to challenge and to try and win the Premier League,” Martínez said. “I know the talent we have up front. I try to bring that solidity at the back.”

"Yalcouye with a sumptuous volley!"Malick Yalcouye puts Brighton on the scoreboard with a venomous volley 😳 pic.twitter.com/8UeeyvPjUw

Conte’s Chelsea had N’Golo Kanté to mop up in midfield and that is an area of the pitch that is causing Alonso some difficulties. Manchester City target Enzo Fernández was once again left out of the squad and Moisés Caicedo was not deemed fit enough to start.

Caicedo was eventually thrown on when Chelsea were trying to stop Brighton completing a remarkable comeback, but he was quickly forced off again with an injury. The club have been exploring a move for Monaco midfielder Lamine Camara and that need looks even more pressing now.

“We want the best for the team and that’s why we took a decision [on Fernández] against Luton and today,” Alonso said. “What’s going to develop? We’re not sure. We can prepare. We are preparing for all the scenarios. But I assure you that whatever happens, from Wednesday [when the transfer window is shut] we’ll have a good enough squad to compete in all the Premier League games.”

Chelsea’s new set-piece coach Austin MacPhee had celebrated Lavia’s goal, which came partly as a result of a corner but owed more to a mistake from Brighton goalkeeper Bart Verbruggen.

MacPhee, however, will not have liked Brighton’s second-half goals. It was from a short corner that the visitors managed to work the ball to Pascal Gross and his cross was diverted into his own net by João Pedro.

Joao Pedro puts Pascal Groß's cross into his own net and Brighton have brought it back to 3-2 👀 pic.twitter.com/maBMwVu3DC

Gross’s headed third goal also came at the end of a set-piece, but, fortunately for Chelsea, it was in the sixth minute of added time and Cole Palmer had already made the points safe for the home team before then.

Palmer had done little to impress watching England head coach Thomas Tuchel until he picked up the ball in the 74th minute, shrugged off two Brighton challenges and produced a brilliant finish to beat Verbruggen.

Cole Palmer finishes EXPERTLY to give Chelsea their two-goal cushion back 💥 pic.twitter.com/6xI9W8xe2q

Fabian Hürzeler, the Brighton manager, said his team “dominated” the game, but acknowledged: “I think if you spend so much money on these kinds of players, like Rogers, Palmer or João [Pedro], then, of course, a team like Chelsea can rely on this individual quality. And they showed it in certain moments of the game.”

Palmer, João Pedro and Rogers are clearly going to be a huge problem for Chelsea’s opponents. But Alonso’s team cannot rely on having to score three or four goals to win games. And they might need to have a bit more of the ball.

"The game today was a special game for me." João Pedro says he was happy with his performance for Chelsea against Brighton 🔵 pic.twitter.com/fWSqWo7ert

6 - João Pedro today was the sixth player (and first for Chelsea) to score a goal, assist a goal, and score an own goal in the same Premier League game, and first since Tottenham Hotspur's Son Heung-min against Man City in December 2023.Eventful. pic.twitter.com/xRVjqkOY9D

There is no time for Brighton to push for the equaliser as the final whistle is blown at Stamford Bridge. Chelsea make it two wins from two to start the new Premier League season but were pushed all the way by Brighton. It finishes 4-3 at Stamford Bridge.

It could well be the last touch of the game but Brighton have a small amount of hope as Gross heads past Martinez. If that had come a few minutes ago, maybe Brighton could have pushed for a draw.

Brighton have a corner and if they are to have any chance of potentially rescuing a point, they have to score right now. De Cuyper’s inswinger is clipped into a dangerous area but for some odd reason referee Michael Oliver gives Chelsea a free-kick. Boscagli is booked for bringing down Rogers.

Double change for Brighton as Costinha and David replace Wieffer and Kostoulas.

Dunk is in trouble. The ball is played forward by Gusto down the right channel to pick out the run of Pedro into the Brighton half. Dunk brings Pedro down but is fortunate that Vuskovic was covering so that is why there is no red card. Dunk is rightly booked.

Chelsea are on the ropes at the moment and Brighton can sense another goal. Boscagli is the latest Brighton player to have an effort and Martinez is forced into a decent save down to his left.

Xabi Alonso is going to respond to the Brighton momentum with a triple change. James, Acheampong and Caicedo replace Neto, Lavia and Fofana.

It is all Brighton and Chelsea are seriously wobbling. Gomez has his fourth chance of the second half and is not far off scoring as his effort hits the side netting. You can sense the anxiety inside Stamford Bridge and it is the travelling Brighton fans making all the noise.

This game is well and truly back on. Chelsea looked in complete control at 3-0 up but now there is just one goal in it. Brighton work a corner short and appear to have wasted the chance but Yalcouye slides a wonderful pass into the right side of the box to pick out the run of Gross, whose shot/cross takes a big deflection off former Brighton man Pedro and goes past Martinez into the Chelsea net.

Joao Pedro puts Pascal Groß's cross into his own net and Brighton have brought it back to 3-2 👀 pic.twitter.com/maBMwVu3DC

Gomez has already missed two chances in this second half and he now has his third opportunity since the break. His powerful effort from the right side of the box forces Martinez into a decent save at his near post...

England head coach Thomas Tuchel is at Stamford Bridge today. He won’t have like Cole Palmer’s miss much and Palmer is probably the only Chelsea attacking player not to have impressed so far. There’s still time, though.

Chelsea have two big chances to score a fourth but cannot take either. First, Neto takes advantage of poor defending from Kadioglu and has a shot saved at the near post by Verbruggen. Then Palmer has a glorious opportunity inside the six-yard box from Rogers’ cross but somehow Palmer guides it over the bar. I am going to say it now that I do not think we have seen an end to the goals today.

Fofana is rightly booked for an earlier challenge on De Cuyper as he completely took him out and Brighton now have a free-kick deep into the Chelsea half after a foul by Neto.

Boscagli clips a lovely free-kick to the back post, where he perfectly picks out Gomez, who has a free header from the edge of the six-yard box but his powerful header goes wide of the far post. That should have been a goal and that is a mighty let-off for Chelsea.

Gomez has a decent chance for Brighton on the edge of the Chelsea penalty area but he fires his effort well wide.

Chelsea attack from back to front, with Martinez launching a long ball forward from inside his own box to pick out the run of Pedro into the Brighton half. Pedro ends up having a shot blocked inside the Brighton penalty area.

Palmer was very influential for Chelsea at Fulham on Monday night and, despite Chelsea scoring three first-half goals, he has been quiet today.

We are back under way at Stamford Bridge. Despite Chelsea being two goals ahead, it does not feel like Brighton are out of this one.

Chelsea go in 3-1 at half-time, having only had 29.3 per cent of possession. They finished with about 35 per cent possession in the 3-2 victory over Fulham, so it seems Alonso is setting his team up very much as a counter-attacking side. It’s all very Antonio Conte.

Vuskovic has a late effort in the first half from range and it goes just over Martinez’s bar.

The Brighton fans enjoy an audacious Pedro backheel that does not come off. Moments later, Gross clips in a cross from the right that picks out Gomez in the box but his header goes over the bar.

There will be two added minutes at the end of this first half.

Pedro has a shot blocked inside the Brighton area before Rogers also has an effort blocked.

The Brighton fans had also been giving the club’s former striker Joao Pedro some stick. Pedro celebrated his goal right in front of them. Touche.

Xabi Alonso takes charge of his first home Premier League game in charge of Chelsea as they host Brighton at Stamford Bridge. Both sides were in action in two different competitions on Thursday night. Chelsea reached the League Cup third round as they beat Luton 2-0 at Stamford Bridge, with former Brighton man Danny Welbeck scoring on his debut. Brighton meanwhile confirmed their place in the Conference League group stages with a 4-0 aggregate win over Tromso.

Chelsea began their Premier League campaign last Monday in a west London derby against Fulham at Craven Cottage, winning 3-2 in Alonso’s first game as Chelsea boss. Enzo Fernandez was not involved in Chelsea’s squad against Luton on Thursday and has been heavily linked with a move to Manchester City. Alonso was asked about Enzo’s absence on Thursday and did not confirm whether the Argentine would be involved today.

“It was just because of the game today [on Thursday] and we have other players who need minutes,” Alonso said. “[On Wednesday], in the afternoon. It is a decision that I took. Enzo is a good professional. He is training well and I have nothing to say about this. It was just decisions that we have to take thinking about the game that we were playing tonight [Thursday]. We will see for Sunday [today].”

Brighton began their Premier League campaign in emphatic style as they thrashed Aston Villa 4-0 at home seven days ago. Jack Hinshelwood scored twice in that game but will now miss a number of weeks with an ankle injury. They are also without Yankuba Minteh, who has been linked with a move to Liverpool this summer but is unavailable due to injury.

“When the window is closed I demand from him [Minteh] that he is fully committed to this club,” Brighton boss Fabian Hurzeler said. “There are dreams and wishes for players, but in the end we always need to figure out what is best for the club.

“We have had an exchange with him. At the moment he is definitely a Brighton player. It is very important to understand his thoughts but also our planning. As a club we try to develop players. The last few years have shown that the whole environment gave him a lot of trust and belief that he is capable of having this progress. It is always a give and take and he has gotten a lot from us.”

Brighton won both Premier League meetings last season, winning 3-1 in this fixture last September. Brighton have won five of their last eight top-flight meetings with Chelsea. Team news from Stamford Bridge to follow shortly.

#1939. ‘Exceptional’ - Former Leeds and Man City man shares bold Brighton and Arsenal title prediction

Former Leeds United man Danny Mills believes 'exceptional' Brighton can achieve Champions League football this season.

The Seagulls have emerged as surprise title contenders this term and are currently second, five points adrift of leaders Arsenals.

Fabian Hurzeler's Brighton are the leading scorers in the division with 26 goals from 10 matches. They have also been impressive at the back with seven clean sheets from 10 matches.

Mills, speaking to BOYLE Sports, who offer the latest football odds, said: "Brighton would need a little bit of luck, possibly with injuries. We've seen Leicester do it in the past.

"Are they likely to win it? Probably not. But is Europa League or Champions League football a possibility with the league the way it is in flux at the moment. Absolutely.

"[Brighton] are incredibly well coached. If you listen to some of the best players that I've ever been around, the likes of Paul Scholes, Nicky Butt, that have seen these up first hand and seen some of the coaching that Fabian Hurzeler is doing, it's exceptional.

"It's clear, it's concise, they have a specific plan that they work to, and it's working for them. I think they will keep it up but they will be tested at some point.

"Undoubtedly there will be a dip at some point within that. But at the moment they're playing with great confidence in what they're doing, great confidence and belief in their manager."

Mills was also full of praise for Brighton transfer model and the fact they give new players and youngsters a chance to shine on the biggest stage.

"I think we've seen in recent years the business model has changed somewhat. I think you have to look at it, you know, teams understand now that bringing in young players and making them better, EPPP ripped the heart out of the academy system, really.

“So all the top clubs took all the best young players very, very early and clubs were not getting huge fees for them at that stage. So I think what they're trying to do now is hold on to these players a little bit longer, develop these players, give themselves a chance.

“I think we've seen it across the leagues, that's the model. It's going back to maybe the old days of let's give players an opportunity, let's give them plenty of game time, improve them, and then sell them on and keep doing the same thing.

“It's no different from the Brentford model, the Brighton model. It's exactly what they're doing. So then identification and recruitment in all that is absolutely key.”

#1938. Newhaven halt Robins’ flight towards play-off place

The Dockers flew out of the traps and would have been ahead with barely a minute on the clock were it not for a great save from the Hassocks keeper to keep out a Matt Gunn header.

Within a minute, Gunn had gone close with another header, before a brilliant Harry Reed cross narrowly evaded the onrushing Tyler Capon.

Did you know with an ad-lite subscription to SussexWorld, you get 70% fewer ads while viewing the news that matters to you.

Thomas Sekyere then went close before Hassocks mustered their first attempt on target; young keeper Jake Rhodes, making his senior debut in Pike’s absence, pulling off a great save from close-range to keep the score goalless.

Newhaven soon resumed control of proceedings, with Matt Feeney-Hill drawing a save from the keeper, before Lee Robinson headed a pin-point Sekyere cross wide of the post.

Despite the game being open and flowing, it took until just after the hour mark for the first goal to arrive.

With 63 minutes on the clock, a Sekyere ball over the top set Robinson away, and he produced a sublime rasping finish from a tight angle to fire the hosts into a deserved lead.

Seven minutes later, it was two as Robinson notched his second. Hassocks failed to fully clear a set-piece, Ross Barclay hooked the ball back into the danger zone, Gunn won a header, and Robinson produced a fine finish on the turn to double the Docker’s advantage.

There was to be no coast to the finish line for Newhaven, though, with the Robins roaring back into the game in the last 20 minutes.

Harvey Blake was inches away from pulling a goal back, with his well-struck effort cannoning off the upright, before Lewis Finney found space in a crowded penalty area to curl the ball beyond the grasp of Rhodes with 13 minutes of normal time left.

Aside from a Robinson effort that was smothered away by the Hassocks custodian, the final stages were largely played out in Newhaven’s defensive half.

With two minutes left of normal time remaining, the visitors seemed almost certain to complete their comeback when a loose ball fell kindly to Finney just inside the six-yard box, only for him to be denied by another superb close-range save by Rhodes.

However, the Dockers managed to cling onto what were a hard-fought but fully-deserved and mightily impressive three-points.

They now look to build on that victory this weekend when Lancing, themselves boosted by a 5-0 win at the weekend, visit Fort Road.

#1937. Derby agendas for Barnsley FC, Bradford City, Doncaster Rovers, Huddersfield Town and Sheffield Wednesday

Barnsley and Doncaster Rovers - down among the dead men in League One - will be hoping that rings true as they seek precious shafts of light following arduous autumns.

They face back-to-back derbies in their next two fixtures, which will assume importance not just for the morale of each club, but also for Daniel Stendel and Grant McCann in their second spells at the Reds and Rovers.

Did you know with a Digital subscription to Yorkshire Post, you can get access to all of our premium content, as well as benefiting from fewer ads, loyalty rewards and much more.

Sheffield Wednesday, Bradford City and Huddersfield Town have their own motivations to contend with.

In the second half of last autumn, Barnsley slipped up at home to Rotherham United, who won in the league at Oakwell for the first time in 15 visits since March 1969. But they did afford themselves the fillip of three points at Doncaster 14 days later.

The Reds, who welcome the Owls on Friday before visiting Bradford - managed by ex-boss Michael Duff - next Tuesday, would probably settle for a 50 per cent derby ratio this time around.

More especially given that their grim winless league run - nine matches and counting - has descended into a crisis.

They must make do without top-scorer and suspended captain Cameron McGeehan on Friday, while defender Jack Shepherd, a boyhood Wednesdayite, is also banned. The return of Patrick Kelly from international duty with Northern Ireland is a much more welcome development.

The sight of in-form Owls striker and Reds old boy Davis Keillor-Dunn compounding their autumnal angst certainly wouldn't be.

A match-winning display from DKD - who has struck in his last three Wednesday matches - would put the tinlid on things for Reds followers, whose expectation levels are exceedingly low heading into Friday.

If things turn sour, the mood in the home stands has the potential to turn mutinous towards the club hierarchy. Barnsley are without a league win since September 2 and are only kept off the bottom of the table by goal difference. A protest from fans group Tykes Union is planned beforehand.

Derbies brought out the best in McCann's Rovers in League One last season and their recent 2-0 win over Wednesday keeping to that theme.

Rovers secured a derby double against arch-rivals Rotherham for the first time since 1949-50 and made history by winning league games at Barnsley and Millers in the same season.

McCann's side also beat Town and Bradford at home and performed very well in both away games and were extremely unlucky to lose both.

They visit the Bantams on Saturday, seeking to get back onside with supporters following dreadful away performances in their last two matches in league and cup - an embarrassing 3-0 FA Cup loss at non-league Kidderminster and an equally atrocious 6-1 league beating at MK Dons.

On both occasions, McCann issued an apology to travelling fans with some starting to openly question his future. The Rovers chief, whose side host high-flying Town next Thursday, prides himself as being a fighter.

Wednesday’s derby form this term has been in keeping with their wretched numbers on that count over the past couple of years.

They have won just once in their past 14 league fixtures against White Rose counterparts.

So far this season, they were bullied in the second half of their meeting with Bradford in their opening home league fixture of 2026-27 - a 1-0 defeat which was more emphatic than the scoreline sounded.

By common consent, they were somewhat fortunate to secure a late point at Huddersfield on October 10 - when Town were very much the architects of their own downfall.

A fortnight later, a disjointed, unsatisfactory performance at Doncaster proved the final straw for the Owls hierarchy regarding Henrik Pedersen.

Historically, Oakwell at least provides rather happier memories for the Owls, notwithstanding their last visit. They have lost just once on their last eight trips up the A61.

After dismal displays - not just results - in three derby losses at Valley Parade, the Club Doncaster Sports Village and Oakwell last season, redressing the balance would be a barometer of Town’s progress in 26-27.

It’s a case of so far, so good with the Terriers avenging last season’s anaemic loss at Bradford with a cathartic victory on Hallowe’en. Statistically speaking, the visitors’ 3-0 triumph was their biggest ever at BD8.

They have two other scores to settle. Town were fitful in their 3-1 defeat at Oakwell last August and it was a sign of things to come for ex-head coach Lee Grant. They visit Barnsley on December 19.

There were jeers and opprobrium following a tepid 1-0 reverse in Doncaster on a February night when Town’s top-six pitch was exposed.

The present-day worries belong to Rovers. And Barnsley.

#1936. Horsham FC ‘well worthy’ of FA Trophy success over Torquay

James Hammond’s 21st minute spot-kick proved to be the difference as the Hornets beat the Gulls 1-0 at home on Saturday.

In an end-to-end Trophy tie, Horsham hit the woodwork three times in the first half and had plenty of opportunities in the second.

Did you know with an ad-lite subscription to SussexWorld, you get 70% fewer ads while viewing the news that matters to you.

Torquay saw a fine effort superbly saved by Hornets stopper Sam Howes before clattering the crossbar – but Horsham held on to advance to the third round.

Di Paola told us: “It was a good game. I thought we played well. I thought we were dominant for 75 minutes of the game and then they came at us. They kept bringing on good players to try to get back into the game.

“I thought we were well worthy of the win for our first half performance if nothing else. We should have been further ahead over the course of the game. Meeky [Reece Myles-Meekums] has had a good chance to kill it at the end, but they’re a good side and we’re happy to get the win.

“When the draw came through you’re thinking, oh no! It was almost a head in hands sort of thing – but the boys have done really well to go through.

“It’s a bit of extra money for the club, so it was all good. It was a really good performance, so we’ve got to be happy with that one.”

The Hornets, who picked up £3,750 for the win, will host Isthmian North outfit Hashtag United in the next round on Saturday, December 12 – and the tie will invoke fond memories for Horsham supporters.

Needing to beat Hashtag and score two more goals than title rivals Billericay Town on the final day of the 2024-25 Isthmian Premier season, the Hornets thumped the Tags 5-1 to leapfrog Ricay on goal difference and secure promotion to the National League South.

Di Paola added: “We’ve had a lot of away draws in the cups this year so I was quite pleased. We’ve had Walton [& Hersham], Plymouth [Parkway, both in the FA Cup], Pagham [in the Sussex Senior Cup] – a few stinkers in terms of away journeys – so I’m just happy to get a home draw.

“I’m sure they’ll come down and be bang up for it. I briefly had a look at the Isthmian North table and they’re having a good season.

“I think they took voluntary relegation last year, but that seems like it’s worked for them. They’re a step three team playing at step four which always helps.

“But a home draw is all you can ever ask for. We’ll park it for a couple of weeks, but I’m just glad to be through to be honest.

“It’s another game, which is a challenge for a small squad, but it got us the prize money and the prize money is important.”

Horsham visit Dover Athletic in National League South this Saturday before welcoming Truro City on Tuesday.

#1935. ‘I think he’s the future’ - Leeds United and England star James Trafford gets Steven Gerrard seal of approval

Leeds United star James Trafford has been described as “the future” of England’s goalkeeping department by Premier League and Three Lions icon Steven Gerrard.

Everton’s Jordan Pickford has spent the bulk of the last decade as England’s first choice but is being pushed hard by Trafford.

Did you know with a Digital subscription to Yorkshire Post, you can get access to all of our premium content, as well as benefiting from fewer ads, loyalty rewards and much more.

Playing time has been evenly split between the pair across the last two international breaks and Trafford was given the gloves against Spain on Sunday (November 15).

He delivered a stellar display in the 3-2 Nations League win, intensifying calls for him to replace Pickford as the number one.

Gerrard told The Overlap Daily: “I really like Trafford, I think he’s the future. But I also like Pickford. I don’t think we can sit here after one performance and dismiss Pickford.

“We’ve probably got two England number ones and the manager’s just got the big decision and that’s why he gets the big bucks. But the future’s Trafford. I think that’s healthy.

“I don’t like it when it’s just a foregone conclusion. He’s the England number one and it doesn’t matter how he plays because he’s the outright number one. Why can’t there be competition, why can’t there be healthy competition?”

Trafford produced a stunning double save in the dying embers, enabling England to hang on and secure a valuable victory over the reigning world champions.

Gerrard said: “It made us win the game. It’s as good or as important as a goal. The second save is world class. There was also a shot straight after it which bounced just in front of him on a greasy surface and it was just like velcro.

“It just stuck to his body. I was really impressed with that as well. It looked simple on the TV but you see so many goalkeepers spill them or want to push them away. He’s just like velcro.”
